stories.Summary:
A demonstration against AI data centers and Big Tech expansion took place in front of Microsoft's data center in Lille Skensved, Denmark, on Nov. 7, according to a Reuters photo published by the Korea JoongAng Daily. The Democrats won sweeping victories in the U.S. midterm elections, which was followed by market turmoil and a plunge in AI-related stocks. Jeong Gwa-ri, a literary critic and honorary professor at Yonsei University, wrote the opinion piece published November 18, 2026. AI companies have raced to expand data centers while communities across America have protested noise, higher electricity bills and damage to their surroundings. The piece was originally written in Korean and translated by a bilingual reporter with the help of generative AI tools, then edited by a native English-speaking editor.

Jeong cites Adam Smith's "The Wealth of Nations" from 1776 and Karl Marx's "Capital" from 1867 on prior accumulation of food and raw materials. He notes the French Revolution of 1789 overthrew feudalism, but the division between capital and labor became unmistakable only during the June uprising of 1848. Marx attacked Pierre-Joseph Proudhon's "The Philosophy of Poverty" from 1846 in "The Poverty of Philosophy" from 1847. Fernand Braudel wrote much of his doctoral research from memory while imprisoned in Germany during World War II, and his "The Mediterranean and the Mediterranean World in the Age of Philip II" from 1949 reconstructed Mediterranean commerce through geographical, social and event-based time. Félix Guattari's "Schizoanalytic Cartographies" from 1989 described a process he called "chaosmos."

Jeong argues the priority should not be suppressing data centers but preventing a small minority from monopolizing their benefits. He says this requires attention to ownership, participation and the distribution of gains throughout society, not technology alone. He writes that AI advances depend not only on a handful of hyperscalers but also on users and their support. He says users should assert their rights while finding ways to participate in AI development, and that Proudhon's proposed people's bank offers one possible reference point. He writes that citizens have both the right and the responsibility to draw creative order from chaos.

Jeong writes that Marx missed a distinction between initial accumulation and the formation of capitalist power, and that most revolutionaries had been small producers: artisans, shopkeepers and independent farmers. He says small producers' spirit passed to white-collar workers, the new middle class and later entrepreneurial founders of modern ventures. He says Braudel distinguished the vibrant market from capitalism, through which large fortunes and state power exert control over people. He writes that capitalists employ labor while small producers work themselves, and that their way of life survives among writers and artists. He says innovation requires tremendous effort, including from investors and business owners.

A second article by a Brandcom partner published November 17, 2026 at 10:00 GMT says South Africa's Draft National Artificial Intelligence Policy was developed and subsequently withdrawn. It says South Africa's municipalities manage electricity and water infrastructure against ageing networks, financial constraints, revenue losses and increasing service delivery demands. Macrocomm is described as a South African technology developer with 21 years of experience in IoT, integrated systems and technology innovation. Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana, in his October 2026 Medium-Term Budget Policy Statement, announced an additional R3.5 billion over the Medium-Term Expenditure Framework for wider rollout of smart meters, over and above the R2 billion previously allocated. The Minister highlighted improved revenue collection in municipalities including Sol Plaatje, Kannaland and Bela-Bela.

Macrocomm has participated in the National Treasury RT29 transversal smart metering programme alongside Vodacom Business and Ontec. In the Sol Plaatje Local Municipality project in the Northern Cape, more than 15,000 smart electricity meters were installed in fewer than 80 days, 85 local residents were trained and employed, and more than 1,200 previously non-billing households were reactivated. Reporting by MyBroadband citing the municipality's General Manager cited an average monthly revenue increase of approximately R5 million. In Naledi Local Municipality in the North West, more than 6,000 smart meters were deployed, and reporting in September 2026 highlighted a reduction in electricity losses from 26% to 5%. The wider programme has also extended to municipalities including Mogale City and Matzikama, with further deployments involving Mbomb.

stories.Headline: South Korea plans unannounced disaster alerts during exam to catch AI-assisted cheaters
stories.Summary:
The government is considering sending unannounced disaster alert messages during this week's annual college entrance exam to catch cheaters using their phones and prevent cheating assisted by artificial intelligence, an interior ministry official said Wednesday. Authorities have been mulling measures to root out cheating during the College Scholastic Ability Test on Thursday following a recent cheating scandal in the certified tax accountant exam using AI. As part of anti-cheating measures unveiled Tuesday, the government said it would send an emergency alert message, designed to reach most mobile phones and sound a loud alarm even when muted, before the start of the exam to detect any unsubmitted devices. The official said the government is considering sending alerts unannounced in addition to the planned alert scheduled to be sent between 8:25 and 8:30 a.m.

President Lee Jae Myung said Tuesday he had instructed authorities to review sending additional alerts, even during testing, to catch cheaters. The government will send another disaster alert at an unspecified time during this week's annual college entrance exam to catch cheaters using their phones and prevent cheating assisted by artificial intelligence, the interior ministry said Wednesday. While the first alert will be sent at 8:30 a.m., just before the start of the test, the ministry plans to send another message at an undisclosed time to find any test takers with unsubmitted phones, according to the ministry. The ministry said the alerts will ring for 10.5 seconds at full volume, urging the public not to be alarmed.

The education ministry notified schools nationwide Wednesday that it will allow test takers to only bring in pencils inside CSAT exam rooms, revising its list of permitted items, according to sources. Authorities earlier notified test takers that they were allowed to bring black marker pens, correction tape, erasers, pencils and mechanical pencil lead for the exam. Under the revised rules, stationery items, except for pencils, will be provided at the test sites. The move appears to reflect concerns of misconduct involving miniature cameras hidden inside personal items brought by test takers.

South Korea has recently been rocked by the recent confession of the top scorer on this year's certified tax accountant exam that he had cheated with the help of AI and digital devices. The incident has deepened worries of such cheating on the upcoming CSAT, widely seen as a major life event in South Korea, where the university one goes to can heavily influence career prospects. President Lee Jae Myung on Tuesday ordered additional measures to curb AI-assisted cheating during Thursday's college entrance exam, a proposed reward of at least 100 million won ($75,000) for tips. More to follow.

stories.Headline: Memphis directs $3.26 million in SpaceX AI data center revenue into South Memphis home repairs and community grants
stories.Summary:
The City of Memphis announced a major investment on November 18, 2026, using its new Community Benefits Ordinance. This plan pumps 3.26 million dollars in revenue from the SpaceX AI Colossus 1 facility back into the city. The funds specifically target various initiatives within the South Memphis neighborhoods located around the data center. This represents the first major investment made under the city's specific ordinance for community benefits. The revenue comes from taxes generated by the operational SpaceX AI data center facility.

The total allocation of 3,259,282 dollars includes 2 million dollars for the Memphis HOPE Initiative home repair program. This program offers low and moderate income homeowners and renters up to 25,000 dollars for qualifying improvements. Eligible work includes structural, plumbing, heating, air conditioning, roof, accessibility, and exterior repairs like painting and fencing. Other funds include 309,282 dollars for community grants, 250,000 dollars for cleanup jobs, and 250,000 dollars for demolitions. Additional amounts cover blight mitigation, air quality equipment, environmental education, health care grants, and Memphis City Beautiful.

City officials are responsible for the fund and stated it will support housing, neighborhood improvements, and local services. They explained that the HOPE Initiative helps residents make vital repairs to make their homes more accessible. The city will provide these funds as deferred, interest-free, and forgivable loans with zero monthly payments. Any required lien on the property will be recorded after repairs are finished and forgiven after three years. These measures aim to directly benefit the residents living in the neighborhoods surrounding the data center.

Low and moderate income residents of South Memphis are the primary people affected by this new funding. The program specifically helps those who need structural repairs or improvements to their home accessibility and safety. The community grants will support public safety, youth, and workforce development services for the local population. Paid neighborhood cleanup and beautification jobs will provide employment opportunities for people in the area. These investments aim to mitigate blight and improve the overall air quality for the local residents.

The Colossus 1 data center became fully operational in May 2025 with 300 megawatts of compute capacity. It contains 220,000 GPUs and was later leased entirely to Anthropic in May 2026 to ease bottlenecks. Anthropic stated this compute would increase API request limits for Claude Opus and remove throttling for Pro customers. Meanwhile, SpaceX AI CEO Elon Musk told employees the company will increase power capacity to 10 gigawatts. This expansion is planned for late 2027 and could generate between 300 billion and 500 billion dollars annually.

The city will now begin distributing the allocated millions for home repairs and various community grants. SpaceX AI will work toward the goal of increasing its data center power capacity by late 2027. The articles leave open how the market capitalization drop of 570 billion dollars affects SpaceX's future plans. It remains unclear how many residents will successfully apply for the 25,000 dollar home improvement loans. The text does not state when the specific neighborhood cleanup and beautification jobs will actually begin.

stories.Headline: Einsia AI releases Visual Cipher Bench to test long-horizon visual reasoning in AI agents
stories.Summary:
Einsia AI's Navers Lab announced the launch of Visual Cipher Bench on November 18, 2026, in Singapore to evaluate long-horizon visual reasoning. This new benchmark tests if AI agents can solve complex problems when instructions are absent and rules must be discovered from visual clues. The evaluation focused on rule discovery, logical planning, and spatial operations across eight frontier models and 29 different reasoning configurations. Researchers recorded 3,480 attempts, but no configuration achieved accuracy above 30 percent, revealing a significant gap in autonomous rule discovery. The top performing model, GPT-6 Astra (max), achieved an accuracy of 26.7 percent, averaging 10.7 correct answers per 40-puzzle run.

The benchmark requires agents to solve 40 original visual puzzles represented by 67 black-and-white illustrations across four distinct reasoning categories. These categories include spatial operations like folding and rotation, logical planning, rule induction for hidden patterns, and knowledge decoding for Braille or Morse. Agents receive only one instruction to examine the images and write the final answer to a file without any immediate correctness feedback. The test includes models like GPT-6.1 Sol, Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5, GPT-6 Luna, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, Qwen 3.8 Max, and Kimi K3.1 Pro. These models must independently identify examples, understand the target problem, infer the required output, and solve each task using only visual evidence.

Deyao Hong and 14 other authors are responsible for the research and the resulting paper titled Visual Cipher Bench: Benchmarking LLM Agents. The researchers stated that the primary bottleneck for current agents is not executing multi-step plans, but autonomously discovering rules from visual evidence. They noted that some correct answers resulted from thematic guesses rather than systematic rule discovery, which skewed some of the results. The authors explained that agents often adopted rules that explained only some examples without validating them against all available evidence before submitting. They also found that agents frequently relied on exhaustive combinations and extensive tool calls instead of using visual constraints, leading to timeouts.

The findings affect frontier AI agents, which struggled significantly with rule induction, achieving an accuracy of only 0.6 percent across all attempts. DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, Qwen 3.8 Max, and Kimi K3.1 Pro failed to solve any puzzles, while GPT-6 Luna and Claude Sonnet 5.5 scored 0.8 percent. GPT-6.1 Sol and Claude Opus 5.5 both scored 21.7 percent, while spatial operations were more manageable with a 22.8 percent accuracy. Knowledge decoding and logical planning were also difficult, recording accuracies of 3.3 percent and 2.4 percent respectively across the 3,480 attempts. Even the best model, GPT-6 Astra, failed to exceed 13.3 percent accuracy in any category other than spatial operations during the tests.

The articles explain that language-model agents typically excel at coding tasks because they have explicit text specifications and immediate execution feedback. Real-world problems often lack these conditions, as critical information may exist only in images that resist text transcription or trial-and-error feedback. Existing visual benchmarks often reduce tasks to single-turn question answering, while agent benchmarks focus on text-based environments or interactive states. This creates a gap because agents must observe environments, identify signals, and formulate hypotheses without explicit instructions to solve autonomous problems. Visual Cipher Bench was created to bridge this gap by measuring the ability to transfer long-horizon capability from text to visual reasoning.

Next, researchers conducted a hint experiment on 10 puzzles using GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol, and GPT-6 Luna to test rule execution. Providing a one-sentence mechanism hint raised overall accuracy from 12.2 percent to 51.1 percent and rule induction accuracy from 0 percent to 85.2 percent. GPT-6 Astra improved from 23.3 percent to 70.0 percent, while GPT-6.1 Sol increased from 13.3 percent to 66.7 percent with these hints. The articles leave open how agents can improve their autonomous rule discovery without hints, as logical planning accuracy remained low at 22.2 percent. They also leave open how to eliminate premature conclusions and inefficient search patterns to move toward more autonomous AI problem-solving.

stories.Headline: Google spends heavily on AI and rebuilds search as rivals challenge its dominance
stories.Summary:
In late October, Alphabet released its most recent earnings report, and the company's stock price plummeted more than 12% the next day, the biggest single-day percentage decline since Google went public in 2004. The Planet Money newsletter asked whether Google had been caught in the innovator's dilemma. Google became one of the most valuable companies in the world by revolutionizing how humanity finds information, and a new generation of AI rivals is now challenging its dominance and pushing Google to spend a fortune to secure its future. Former Google executive Marissa Mayer remembers when the company was a scrappy startup working out of a small office above a bike shop in Palo Alto, Calif. She joined Google in 1999, fresh out of nearby Stanford with a master's in computer science, and became its 20th employee.

When Mayer interviewed at Google there were just seven people there, and by the time she got hired, a month or two later, she became its 20th employee. That year, Google brought in just over $200,000 in annual revenue, and by 2022, the eve of the AI boom, the company, by then reorganized under a parent company called Alphabet, was generating more than $280 billion, a more than millionfold increase. Google made its fortune selling ads next to its search results, monopolized internet searches so thoroughly that its name became a verb, and its search business became like an unstoppable money machine. In 2012, Mayer left and became the CEO of Yahoo, trying to revive a competitor that Google had blown out of the water, but neither Yahoo nor any other rival managed to dethrone King Google. Its share of the U.S. search-engine market grew from 80% in 2009 to nearly 90% in 2020.

Google plowed the profits from its search business into research and development of AI, and in 2017 a team of eight Google employees developed the transformer, a breakthrough technology that made today's AI chatbots possible. Mayer, now CEO of the AI startup Dazzle and a Google shareholder, sees Google's pioneering AI work as a reason for optimism, saying this is not a technology that's happening to Google and that they helped invent this new technology. Today Google is spending enormous amounts to build its AI capabilities and fend off rivals, and it is overhauling its search business, using AI to answer questions directly instead of just providing links. The late Harvard Business School professor Clayton Christensen developed the innovator's dilemma theory in his 1997 book, The Innovator's Dilemma: When New Technologies Cause Great Firms to Fail. Christensen theorized that the very thing that makes a business wildly successful can lead to its downfall in the face of a disruptive technology, and he helped put disruption in Silicon Valley's vocabulary long before it became a cliché.

Google's researchers made computers translate languages, recognize speech and images, drive cars autonomously, and even beat one of the world's best players at the game Go, and the company developed an internal chatbot called Meena that employees played with years before AI chatbots became a sensation, but they didn't release it. On Nov. 30, 2022, OpenAI released ChatGPT and offered a completely new way to find information and a glimpse of a future where people didn't need to go to Google to find answers anymore, and Google scrambled to respond, reportedly declaring a "code red" as ChatGPT captivated the masses. Last year, Google's chief scientist, Jeff Dean, told podcaster Dwarkesh Patel that they looked at their existing chatbots through the lens of their search business, saying that from a search perspective you want to get the right answer 100% of the time and that these models were not near that bar. Dean acknowledged that Google had underestimated how useful chatbots could be for things people wouldn't necessarily turn to a search engine for, like drafting a note or summarizing text. Mayer questions whether releasing a chatbot first would have gone as well for Google as it did for OpenAI, saying the standards for an established company like Google in terms of what users expect, in terms of quality, how good the search is, how great the product is, are fundamentally different than for an upstart or a newcomer.

Benedict Evans, a widely read technology analyst previously a partner at the Silicon Valley venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz, says that every 10 or 15 years or so a revolutionary platform shift shakes up the tech industry, giving newcomers a chance to challenge dominant companies, and that it happened with personal computers, then the internet, then smartphones, and now with AI. Evans says the whole table gets reset and the things that meant that they had won and you couldn't take them on suddenly don't matter anymore. The process toward monopolization began with Google building a better search engine than rivals, and then, Evans says, its success became self-reinforcing: more users gave Google more data to improve its results, helping it attract still more users, which economists call a network effect. Google also paid to make its search engine the default in browsers and on devices, deals that a federal judge ruled in 2024 had illegally helped maintain its search monopoly. Google runs the operating system on many of our phones, we use free Google services to send emails, write documents, find directions, and watch a stranger explain how to fix our washing machine, and many of us keep going back to Google search out of sheer habit or because we keep getting nudged to go there.

Google has fought back with its own chatbot, now called Gemini, and by putting AI-generated answers directly onto its search page, even at the risk of undermining the advertising business that made it rich. The question now is whether all this will leave Google as dominant and as profitable in the AI age as it was in the age of old-school web search. Christensen warned in The Innovator's Dilemma that companies that keep disruptive technologies bottled up in their labs risk losing out to rivals willing to run with them, however imperfect they may be. The articles leave open what would have happened if Google had released a chatbot first, whether a Google chatbot would have taken off in the same way and given Google a first-mover advantage, or whether its flaws would have created big headaches for a company with an established reputation to protect. The articles also leave open whether rival AI systems will borrow from Google's playbook and work to intertwine themselves into our lives.

stories.Headline: Roger Holm and Siri-Anne Mjåtvedt say AI strengthens maritime safety and decision making
stories.Summary:
Roger Holm and Siri-Anne Mjåtvedt discussed the integration of artificial intelligence into maritime operations on November 17, 2026. The two leaders shared their insights during a conversation for the Maritime Matters podcast produced by Marinelink. They explored how this transformative technology is being used to enhance safety and efficiency across the maritime sector. The discussion focused on moving beyond trends to implement practical tools that support professionals in the field. This conversation highlighted the evolving role of technology in reshaping how maritime businesses operate and manage their fleets.

The implementation of AI requires a shift toward data driven decisions for voyage planning and predictive maintenance of vessels. Utkilen uses Microsoft Copilot to ensure that all employees can learn and work with these new tools from day one. The company applies AI to automate data collection for vessel positioning and to enhance existing emergency response systems. Wärtsilä invested 329 million euros into research and development last year to combine AI with various decarbonization strategies. These efforts aim to ensure compliance with environmental regulations while improving the overall reliability and uptime for their customers.

Roger Holm, the President Marine at Wärtsilä, stated that the real value of AI is strengthening human decision making. He explained that the technology is meant to integrate people with data in an optimized way rather than replacing jobs. Siri-Anne Mjåtvedt, the CEO of Utkilen, said the company moves forward with AI only if it improves safety or efficiency. She described the company's approach as treating artificial intelligence as a business tool instead of just a technological project. Both leaders believe that combining domain expertise with AI creates more certainty and better operational performance for their clients.

Maritime professionals are affected by these changes as they are empowered to make more informed and data driven decisions. Crew members benefit because the automation of data collection allows them to focus their time on high value tasks. Customers also see improvements through better vessel uptime and the increased efficiency of maritime operations and voyage planning. The broader industry is impacted by the use of AI to meet environmental goals and support global decarbonization efforts. These advancements are designed to benefit the business while ensuring that vessels operate at their peak possible efficiency.

The articles state that the maritime industry has always been at the forefront of adopting new and transformative technologies. AI is now being used to turn complex information into actionable insights that support the industry's sustainability goals. The background provided shows that AI is a game changer that is reshaping the paradigm of maritime business operations. Research and development investments are being used to align technological growth with strict environmental and regulatory requirements. This context positions AI as a vital component of modern operations rather than just a temporary industry buzzword.

The industry will continue to embrace AI to enhance operations and contribute to a more sustainable maritime future. Companies will likely continue the practical implementation of AI tools to improve safety and decision making for their crews. Wärtsilä will continue to use its research and development budget to find innovative solutions for decarbonization and reliability. The articles leave open how other maritime companies will adopt these specific tools or if new technologies will emerge. It remains to be seen how these AI integrations will specifically impact long term employment and global regulatory compliance.

stories.Headline: Wichita Public Schools and Talkmate implement AI tools to personalize student learning
stories.Summary:
Wichita Public Schools began exploring generative artificial intelligence in January 2023 to save teachers time. By April, district leaders shifted their goal toward designing personalized learning experiences for all students. On November 14, Talkmate rolled out an AI agent for learners at the World Chinese Language Conference. A Russian student named Beliaeva Lian used this tool in Beijing to practice her Chinese. Sixty international students from over ten countries also participated in a Chinese learning hackathon.

The Brookings Institution created the Prosper, Prepare and Protect framework to guide schools in using AI. Wichita Public Schools uses grade-banded expectations, starting with simple talks for students in kindergarten through first grade. Students in second through fifth grades have no independent exposure, while those in sixth through eighth use approved tools. High school students critically analyze outputs, and the district follows guidelines from surrounding universities to restrict use. Talkmate launched a mobile AI agent to provide cultural outreach, study tours, and job matching.

Dyane Smokorowski, the digital literacy coordinator, says AI helps design for students in the margins. She believes students still need productive struggle because it is good for their brains and humans. Katelyn Schoenhofer, a technology instructional coach, says AI handles administrative work to free up teachers. He Hongzhi from Capital Normal University says AI provides scientific methods and authentic environments for learners. He believes AI can address the lack of sustained support for those learning the Chinese language.

Beliaeva Lian said she was surprised that the AI could understand her Chinese so accurately. She felt that the Chinese language was not actually that difficult after using the agent. The Brookings Institution notes that AI should deepen learning rather than replace the effort required to learn. Paraprofessionals are now being trained to use AI for one-on-one or small group student support. Families must also be educated to ensure that responsible AI use continues within the home.

Wichita Public Schools wants to avoid the bad habits students developed with previous technology like social media. The district uses scaffolds that are temporary and accommodations that some students will always need. Teachers receive training first so they can model critical thinking skills for their students later. Talkmate is a global partner of UNESCO that promotes a vision called Chinese Made Easy. The mobile agent aims to support learners worldwide at every step of their educational journey.

Wichita Public Schools will continue refining how to measure what is working with their AI tools. Training for paraprofessionals has only just started, so the final outcomes are not yet seen. Smokorowski suggests that districts should collaborate in partnerships rather than exploring these new possibilities alone. The articles do not state if other school districts have adopted the Brookings Institution framework. It remains open whether the Talkmate agent will be adopted by universities in Beijing.

stories.Headline: Nvidia invests billions in supply chain partners to scale AI computing production
stories.Summary:
On Tuesday, November 18, 2026, the American chipmaker Nvidia announced it is expanding manufacturing capacity with several supply chain partners. The company is collaborating with Amkor Technology, Foxconn, Kinsus Interconnect Technology, Samsung Electro-Mechanics, Siliconware Precision Industries, and TSMC to meet long-term demand for artificial intelligence computing platforms. These partnerships aim to scale production across substrates, advanced packaging, wafer manufacturing, and contract manufacturing. This strategic move supports the growth of both current and next-generation accelerated computing platforms.

The expansion involves a multiyear agreement with Siliconware Precision Industries to grow advanced packaging operations in Taiwan by mid-2029. Kinsus Interconnect Technology received over $1 billion from Nvidia to increase advanced ABF substrate capacity at its Taoyuan facility by more than 3.5 times. Production at that site should begin in the second half of 2027, with more capacity arriving in the third quarter of 2028. Samsung Electro-Mechanics will optimize its existing factories, while Amkor Technology expands advanced packaging capacity in South Korea and Arizona.

Nvidia is responsible for these investments and stated that the expanded commitments will support the long-term growth of its AI platforms. Foxconn Chairman Young Liu explained that his company is deepening its collaboration on networking and GPU platforms. He noted that Foxconn will use its global manufacturing network across Europe, North America, and Asia to scale AI infrastructure. These efforts ensure a steady supply of critical components for the company's rapidly growing hardware ecosystem.

The company recently began volume shipments of Vera CPUs and Vera Rubin NVL72 for agentic AI during the third quarter. These specific products utilize CoWoS advanced packaging technology along with the 3-nanometre and 5-nanometre chipmaking processes from TSMC. This rollout marks a significant step in deploying next-generation hardware for complex AI tasks. The company continues to leverage these global partnerships to maintain its lead in the accelerated computing market.

stories.Headline: Karnataka chief minister D K Shivakumar launches six AI and semiconductor initiatives at Bengaluru Tech Summit 2026
stories.Summary:
Karnataka Chief Minister D K Shivakumar launched six initiatives at the Bengaluru Tech Summit 2026, which opened on November 17, 2026, in Bengaluru. The summit runs from November 17 to 19 and is themed "AI & Beyond". The Karnataka AI Hub was officially launched at the summit and is established at IIIT-Bengaluru. The state government had earlier approved a ₹35 crore budget for the Karnataka AI Hub. The summit's exhibitors come from more than 75 countries, according to its official website.

The Karnataka AI Hub will focus on AI research, skilling, innovation and entrepreneurship, and is the first step towards the state's proposed AI University. BRAINZ, the Bengaluru Robotics and AI Innovation Zone, is an envisioned 9-acre facility in collaboration with ARTPARK at the Indian Institute of Science. BRAINZ aims to catalyse investments of ₹1,000 crore over five years. The state is supporting IISc's proposed 200-mm research and pilot-line facility under the 2D Innovation Hub, which includes a technology building of about 100,000 sq ft, a 15,000 sq ft cleanroom and 80 to 90 process, metrology and testing tools. The state is also supporting INFIfab, a proposed national facility for semiconductor fabrication, advanced packaging and technology translation, covering about 96,284 sq ft including a 20,000 sq ft cleanroom, with focus areas including MEMS, photonics, quantum technologies and neuromorphic computing.

K-HEAL is a Centre of Excellence for healthcare, medical and assistive technology, and a flagship programme of the Department of Electronics, IT & BT. Innoverse aims to support 35 growth-stage deeptech ventures over five years, including autonomous systems and technologies from underwater applications to space. Shivakumar said Karnataka laid the foundations of modern industry and technology through institutions of learning and research, strong public sector enterprises and the trust of global companies. He said some of India's most ambitious scientific and engineering projects have found a home in Karnataka. He said, "We will bring the talent, the policies and the partnership.

You bring your ambition." Shivakumar said Karnataka accounted for two out of every five dollars earned by India through software and services exports. He said the state received $9.4 billion in foreign direct investment equity inflows in the first half of FY26, accounting for 26.7% of India's total inflows during the period. He said more than 1,000 global capability centres have established operations in Bengaluru, and the state is home to more than 100 fabless chip companies. He said three out of every five engineers working in India's semiconductor capability centres were based in Bengaluru, and global companies are investing more than ₹23,000 crore in semiconductor research and manufacturing facilities in Bengaluru and Mysuru.

The state is developing four electronics manufacturing clusters from Dharwad to Mysuru. The government announced proposed AI skilling programmes with Google, Salesforce, Pega Systems, Sarvam AI and Gnani.ai, targeting 63,200 engineering and diploma students and professionals. The programmes will cover generative AI, agentic AI, voice AI, cloud computing, data analytics and responsible AI, combining classroom instruction with practical exercises, industry tools, capstone projects and certification pathways. Under the ₹300-crore Nipuna Karnataka reskilling mission, more than 33,000 people have already become industry-ready through partnerships with technology companies. Karnataka is home to more than 24,000 recognised startups, with nearly two out of every five Indian unicorns originating from the state.

Through its ELEVATE programme, the government has supported nearly 1,500 startups with $41 million in equity-free grants over a decade, and under ELEVATE NxT, 33 deeptech startups have received ₹30 crore in grants since last year. The government has allocated ₹25 crore under its Government First initiative to procure innovative solutions developed by startups. Shivakumar said the state accounts for one-fifth of India's bioeconomy, valued at $39.2 billion last year, and the government plans to expand biotechnology into marine resources, agriculture and healthcare. The Karnataka AI Hub aims to develop a globally competitive workforce and facilitate the application of research in practical fields.

BRAINZ will bring together research institutions, industries and startups working in robotics, artificial intelligence and deeptech. The 2D Innovation Hub facility will serve as a shared platform for academic institutions and industry partners to undertake semiconductor research and development. K-HEAL will connect clinicians, researchers, industries and startups to identify unmet healthcare requirements, develop and validate technological solutions and facilitate their adoption. Innoverse will support Karnataka-based deeptech startups that have already developed and validated their technologies and are looking to expand their market presence and global operations.

The articles do not say when the proposed AI University, BRAINZ, the 2D Innovation Hub facility or INFIfab will be built or opened. The articles do not name the cost of BRAINZ, the 2D Innovation Hub facility or INFIfab. The articles do not say which company will run each AI skilling programme or when the training will begin. The articles do not say how the six initiatives will be funded beyond the ₹35 crore approved for the Karnataka AI Hub.

stories.Headline: Anthropic weighs upsizing its IPO as demand surges past $400 billion
stories.Summary:
Anthropic is considering upsizing its initial public offering, according to people familiar with the details, as the artificial intelligence lab weighs setting the price well above $80. The company closed its order books and locked in total demand on Tuesday, setting the stage for the Claude creator's eagerly awaited Nasdaq listing. Anthropic is expected to set its final IPO price after market close Wednesday. The stock is set to begin trading on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol ANT on Thursday. Anthropic will make final decisions Wednesday afternoon, the people said.

The AI lab said last week that it would offer 825 million shares in the IPO at a price range of between $70 and $78 per share, which would net up to $64.35 billion at the high end of that range. Institutional demand for the offering is around $400 billion, while retail demand is approaching $100 billion, according to the people. The orders are indications of interest and are not binding, and all of the details are subject to change. Demand for the offering is higher than it was for Elon Musk's SpaceX, even though the rocket maker had a bigger market offering. SpaceX debuted on the Nasdaq in June in by far the biggest IPO on record, ultimately raising $85.7 billion.

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei said in the company's roadshow video that if done right, "we can create an age of miracles where humanity is able to solve problems that have eluded us for millennia." Amodei said the company has to make sure that all the risks and all the ways things can go wrong with this technology are very carefully addressed as it brings the benefits and has a viable business at the same time. Anthropic's co-founders wrote in the company's prospectus that their aim is to help humankind chart a safe course through this technological evolution, open new frontiers of discovery, and bring forth an age of miracles. The co-founders wrote that everyone who owns the stock, whether an institution or an individual, becomes part of that effort. A representative for Anthropic declined to comment.

Amazon and Google both own stakes in Anthropic valued at over $100 billion, and a group of tech companies, including Google, Microsoft, Nvidia and Advanced Micro Devices, agreed to collectively invest $26 billion in the IPO. Anthropic, meanwhile, is a buyer of costly systems from Nvidia, Google, Amazon and AMD. Anthropic's listing is a major test for the AI industry, which has experienced a set of recent shocks, including a dramatic backlash felt at the polls in the midterm elections and last week's ouster of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. The market was already jittery on concerns that rising interest rates will make debt unaffordable for many data center developers and neoclouds. Anthropic's IPO has reportedly drawn six times too many orders for its available stock shares.

Amodei co-founded Anthropic alongside a handful of other researchers less than six years ago, after the group collectively defected from OpenAI. The company is best known for developing a family of AI models called Claude, and it primarily sells its products and services to other businesses. Anthropic has been racing to maintain an edge over OpenAI and Google in the enterprise market, and it experienced a period of explosive growth in 2026, driven largely by the popularity of its AI coding tool, Claude Code. OpenAI has confidentially filed for an IPO and has said a debut is likely in 2027. Anthropic has faced two high-profile disputes with the U.S. government this year over its positions on safety, regulation and national security.

For the nine months ended Sept. 30, Anthropic said, it generated $33.24 billion in revenue, up roughly 1,200% from the same period last year, according to its prospectus. The company reported a $104 billion net loss during the nine-month period, though most of that was due to the change in fair value of convertible notes and derivative liabilities. Anthropic lost $25.1 billion over the same stretch in 2025, the filing said. Anthropic said in an amended filing that its run-rate revenue was roughly $81 billion at the end of October, up $10 billion from the previous month. Its prospectus included more than 90 pages of risk factors for investors to consider ahead of its IPO.

stories.Headline: Majority of registered voters disapprove of Donald Trump's handling of artificial intelligence
stories.Summary:
A Reuters-Ipsos survey conducted in early November 2026 revealed that 56 percent of registered voters disapproved of how President Donald Trump handled artificial intelligence. Only 26 percent of those surveyed approved of his approach, while 16 percent believed the administration had the risks about right. This polling occurred as the United States competed with China for dominance in the field of rapidly advancing technology. The results highlight growing public fear regarding the societal impact of these systems across different political parties.

The president has favored limited regulation and rebranded the technology as super intelligence during September. He reached a morally binding agreement with technology leaders for voluntary safeguards and company oversight of their own systems. In September, Trump wrote on Truth Social that a strong and smart president served as the only necessary guardrail for the technology. More recently, the Trump administration issued new rules on Monday to restrict remote access to advanced servers and computing chips. These changes follow the resignation of Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang, who faced scrutiny over an affair with a suspected Chinese spy.

CNN chief data analyst Harry Enten stated on Tuesday that the American people do not believe the administration has the right priorities. Enten suggested that Trump is dismissing the concerns of his own base, which may have contributed to depressed Republican turnout during the midterm election. The president defended the voluntary arrangement, telling reporters that he saw tremendous self-policing among tech titans like Mark Zuckerberg and Elon Musk. Trump also described the former Nvidia chief as honorable and claimed Huang was likely unaware of the spy connection.

The context of this disapproval includes warnings from industry leaders like Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, who suggested AI could eliminate half of entry-level white-collar jobs within five years. Some employees at Anthropic have even warned that the technology could potentially kill all humans within the next decade. Public anxiety has also been fueled by recent technical failures in banking, flight traffic, and Apple systems. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy noted on Tuesday that he would inform the public if a recent airline ground stop resulted from an AI attack.

stories.Headline: Microsoft claims MAI Code 2 matches 96% of Claude Opus 5.5 at 5% of the cost
stories.Summary:
Microsoft unveiled a new lineup of specialized AI models at its Ignite conference on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, making a direct run at Anthropic and OpenAI in coding, cybersecurity and image generation. The company pitched models trained to do particular jobs at substantially lower cost instead of one chatbot that beats everyone at everything. The biggest claim involves MAI Code 2, which Microsoft says delivers 96% of Claude Opus 5.5's performance on common enterprise coding tasks for just 5% of the cost. Microsoft also claims 98% of GPT-6.1 Sol's performance at 40% of the price. OpenAI also released GPT-6.2 on Tuesday, so Microsoft's Sol comparison already concerns an older generation.

Those figures average results from four evaluations focused on practical software development, including fixing code and completing multi-file changes. Microsoft ran three of the tests on its own evaluation platform, used outside results for the fourth, and calculated MAI Code 2's costs using a 50% promotional discount. A lighter Code 2 Flash model targets routine fixes and quick edits, with Microsoft claiming performance comparable to Claude Haiku 5.5 at 20% of the price. Microsoft says MAI Cyber 2 Flash succeeded on 92.3% of CyberGym-E2E's evaluated vulnerability-discovery tasks, compared with 91.5% for GPT-6 Astra, at less than 2% of the cost per task. Microsoft excluded 92 of 905 tasks after identifying overlap between their source material and its training data.

Microsoft has not yet published a direct comparison against OpenAI's restricted GPT-6 Cyber model. Its security system will begin replacing an older MAI model for eligible MDASH customers in mid-December, building on the vulnerability-scanning approach Decrypt previously covered. Microsoft's own documentation says Code 2 is not yet optimized for fundamental scientific research or very long-running autonomous assignments. Microsoft quotes about $35 per 1,000 images for MAI Image 2.7 and $10 for its Flash version, versus roughly $211 for GPT Image 2.6 Sunburst at maximum quality in Artificial Analysis's comparison. Microsoft is also offering selected business customers the ability to customize and run its models' licensed weights inside Azure, reducing reliance on outside vendors without making the technology open source.

On Artificial Analysis's image-editing test, which asks people to choose between anonymously generated edits and turns those preferences into an Elo rating, MAI Image 2.7 currently leads with 1,215 points against GPT Image 2.6 Sunburst's 1,211. The four-point gap is small enough that their reported uncertainty ranges overlap, and the separate text-to-image generation ranking puts Microsoft in fourth place. Google's Nano Banana 2.1 is about $34 per 1,000 images there, while Nano Banana Pro is about $134, and actual bills depend on the provider, resolution and settings. Both coding models are already in GitHub Copilot, putting Microsoft's in-house technology directly into a product that has relied heavily on outside AI suppliers. Microsoft also announced MAI Work Flash, which it describes as having been derived from Code 2 Flash and which can help generate formulas in Excel, work with documents and instructions in Word, and track decisions and extract useful information from Teams.

Microsoft famously has a multi-billion-dollar investment in OpenAI dating back to 2023 and has built many of its products and services around OpenAI intellectual property. Anthropic competes in the cheaper end of the market with Haiku, not just its premium Opus models, so Microsoft is entering a race its rivals already understand. OpenAI has taken a related approach with its Mini and Nano models, letting cheaper workers handle routine tasks while larger systems tackle the exceptions. Our earlier testing of MAI Image 2 found excellent realism but frustrating limits on editing and output formats, and the newer release adds interactive editing through Microsoft's Canvas workspace, transparent backgrounds and broader access through Foundry. Microsoft says the numbers it is reporting use a 50% introductory discount, and the benchmarks are all Microsoft-provided.

For the next test of its specialist strategy, Code 2 is already available in GitHub Copilot, and the Cyber 2 Flash rollout is scheduled to start in mid-December. Microsoft is touting that it is integrating these new models as optional choices for GitHub Copilot, Microsoft 365 and Fabric. The company has not yet published a direct comparison against OpenAI's restricted GPT-6 Cyber model. Performance numbers may well differ once the models undergo independent performance tests, and benchmark selection could be cherry-picking. The company also described clearly that these new models are not designed to handle the most challenging agentic and research workloads.

stories.Headline: SAP engineers contribute to Nvidia OpenShell as SAP embeds it in its Business AI Platform
stories.Summary:
SAP and Nvidia are deepening their collaboration to make autonomous AI agents in enterprises safer, more controllable and fully auditable, the companies said, with the open-source secure runtime environment OpenShell to be deeply embedded in the newly consolidated SAP Business AI Platform. Thomas Pfiester, Head of Customer Engagement and Adoption and a member of SAP's Extended Board, presented SAP's vision of the Autonomous Enterprise in a keynote at the 2026 DSAG Annual Congress in Cologne on Tuesday, October 6, and referred to the Nvidia partnership when asked how existing SAP customers keep AI agents under control. Andre Lamego, Senior Vice President and Chief Product Officer for the SAP Business AI Platform Fabric, provided the technical background, and E3 Magazine summarized and supplemented his comments. The announcement covers the Nvidia Open Agent Safety Platform and the widespread availability of Nvidia OpenShell, as previously announced at the SAP Sapphire customer conference.

SAP engineers are contributing directly to the Nvidia OpenShell codebase as part of the co-development effort, while the AI-centric development environment Joule Studio provides a complete execution and governance stack for enterprise agents and Nvidia's OpenShell handles secure deployment and execution within clear security boundaries. SAP's development work focuses on four specific core areas of the OpenShell project: at the platform architecture level SAP has driven the decomposition of the runtime environment into independently deployable components by separating the supervisor layer from the actual agent execution layer to enable isolated scaling. For native Kubernetes operation the contributions include operator support, the management of confidential access data known as image pull secrets for private container registries, customer-specific storage requirements called Custom Volume Claim Templates, and the orderly deletion of sandbox resources. SAP is also working to minimize the environmental and technical footprint of the gateway container image, expand driver support for heterogeneous computing infrastructures, and embed monitoring of the supervisor's operational readiness and structured logging in accordance with established observability standards.

At the governance level the Joule Studio runtime environment serves as the highest authority, checking business authorizations, role-based policies and the relevant process context before a request reaches the actual execution layer, while Nvidia OpenShell complements this with an isolated runtime sandbox that precisely controls what an agent is allowed to see and do and where inference data flows. The collaboration is supported by the goal of achieving FedRAMP and FIPS certifications for regulated industries and by participation in the newly founded Open Secure AI Alliance. SAP is making Joule Studio's runtime environment available to its customers and partners free of charge through the end of October 2026, after which, according to the article, usage-based billing relying on consumption-dependent AI Units, BTP Capacity Units and AI token prices will kick in. The article describes the free period as a classic bait-and-switch tactic common in the software industry and says existing customers fall for a costly illusion if they believe autonomous agents will remain free of charge indefinitely.

stories.Headline: EU study finds Digital Omnibus changes would make it harder for workers to obtain employer data
stories.Summary:
Dublin City Council published a page on 18 November 2026 stating it is committed to fulfilling its obligations under the General Data Protection Regulation. The page explains that people have the right to obtain a copy of any information about them held by Dublin City Council. It says this information could be stored on a computer or in a manual filing system. The page tells people to write to the council to obtain information about themselves. It also offers an email option and a Data Access Request Form to download as a DOCX file of 0.1MB.

The page gives a letter template asking for a copy of any information kept about the person, on computer or in manual form. It asks people to include details that could help locate records, such as a customer account number, a staff number or any other identifying information. It says requests should be accompanied by a copy of official photo identification, such as a passport, a driver's licence or a public services card. It lists contact details for the Information Management Unit at 01 222 3775 and the email address [email protected], at Civic Offices, Wood Quay, Dublin 8, Co. Dublin D08 RF3F, Ireland. It also lists a general telephone number, 01 222 2222, and the email address [email protected].

The page says people may contact the council if they have concerns that a data breach has occurred in relation to their personal data. It says people may also contact the council if their personal data has been put at risk by unauthorised access or disclosure. It says the council will investigate the matter fully and notify the person of the outcome as soon as possible. It says all traffic cameras operated and managed by Dublin City Council are used for traffic monitoring purposes, are live feed only and do not record. It directs people to a map of traffic poles with CCTV to determine whether the camera they are seeking footage from is a traffic camera.

The page says that if the camera in question is included in the map then no recording has taken place and no footage exists. It says that if the camera is not included in the map, people should submit their request to the address noted, providing the specific location of the camera and a copy of valid photo identification. It says the General Data Protection Regulation allows access to information that is personal in nature, so a person will only be entitled to access footage of themselves. It says any third parties captured in footage will be redacted or pixelated before release. It refers people to the website of the Data Protection Commissioner for information on data protection.

Netzpolitik.org reported on 17 November 2026 that the EU Commission proposed the Digital Omnibus without conducting a full impact assessment. It said the Digital Omnibus is currently being discussed in the EU parliament and is a package proposed by the European Commission targeting, among other laws, the General Data Protection Regulation. It said the Commission presents the new framework as a simplification and competitiveness measure and estimates the package could deliver up to €5 billion in administrative cost savings by 2029. It said more than 100 European civil society organizations have called the proposal an attempt to covertly dismantle Europe's strongest protections against digital threats. It said the European Trade Union Institute study was conducted by researchers Aida Ponce Del Castillo and Thomas le Bonniec.

The study applied the amendments counterfactually to four workplace cases that had previously led to regulatory enforcement or successful legal claims against workplace data abuse. In one case, six Uber drivers sought access to personal data and information about how the platform's systems affected their work, including information on matching, pricing and ratings. A similar case was filed against Ola, a ridesharing company based in India. In 2023, the Amsterdam Court of Appeal upheld claims by the drivers and required Uber and Ola to disclose specified personal data and meaningful information about certain automated decision-making systems. The study's authors argue that reaching similar outcomes could become more difficult under the Digital Omnibus changes.

The amendments would create broader grounds for employers or platforms to resist workers' requests for access to their personal data. An employer could argue that a worker was using a GDPR access request for a purpose other than exercising data-protection rights, such as gathering evidence for an employment dispute. According to the study, the changes could shift a greater burden onto workers, who may need to formulate more specific requests, challenge refusals or seek legal assistance simply to obtain information already held by their employer or platform. Study author Aida Ponce Del Castillo of the ETUI in Brussels said a worker may be right about unlawful surveillance and still be unable to prove it. She said that if the EU makes it harder to obtain information from an employer, it also makes it harder for people to challenge what happens to them at work.

In a related case, four Uber drivers challenged the deactivation of their accounts after Uber systems flagged suspected fraudulent activity. The drivers argued that these were consequential decisions made solely through automated processing, without meaningful human intervention. For three of the four drivers in the actual case, the court found that Uber had not demonstrated meaningful human intervention. The drivers had not been heard, and Uber had not shown that its reviewers had sufficient information and authority to change the automated outcome. The GDPR provides protections against certain decisions based solely on automated processing.

Currently, the availability of an equally effective human alternative can be relevant when assessing whether automated processing was really necessary. The proposed amendments would change this test, so the existence of a possible human alternative would no longer, by itself, be enough to argue that automated processing was unnecessary. Applying that change to the Uber case, Uber would be in a stronger legal position, the authors argue, and could argue that automated fraud detection was necessary for performing its contractual relationship with drivers, even if a human could have made the decision instead. The authors conclude that under the proposed changes the legal pathway to comparable outcomes to the Uber and Ola cases would have been narrower. A part of the Digital Omnibus package concerning AI was already adopted in July this year.

That part delayed the application of the AI Act's requirements for high-risk systems by 16 months, until December 2027, including requirements affecting certain AI systems used in employment and worker management. The authors argue the two sets of changes could reinforce each other, with AI Act safeguards taking effect later while changes to the GDPR could make it more difficult for workers to investigate or challenge those practices after they occur. The netzpolitik.org article was published on 17 November 2026 at 15:38. The Dublin City Council page was published on 18 November 2026 at 10:30. The study examined the potential consequences of the Digital Omnibus for workers in the EU.

stories.Headline: US chip restrictions threaten Southeast Asia data centre growth to block Chinese access
stories.Summary:
The United States government recently moved to close a loophole that allegedly allowed China to access powerful chips through artificial intelligence infrastructure in Southeast Asia. This regulatory action follows the resignation of Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang last week after reports surfaced regarding multiple extramarital affairs. One of these relationships involved Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman and former executive at the Singapore-based firm Megaspeed. American media outlets have identified Alice Huang as a suspected spy for the Chinese government.

Washington is now probing Megaspeed while requiring data centre operators to license existing remote compute within a ninety day window. These new restrictions threaten to slow the rapid growth of data centres across Southeast Asia by removing the cover used for chip diversion. The United States is currently working to contain the fallout from this scandal involving a central figure in industry financing. This shift in policy aims to prevent the unauthorized transfer of high-end technology to Chinese entities.

The resignation of Jensen Huang has shocked the AI community because he was a close ally of the White House. Officials are concerned that the relationship between the former chief executive and the suspected spy compromised national security. While the specific details of the probe remain private, the government is focusing on how the region's infrastructure was exploited. The situation highlights the vulnerability of global supply chains to personal scandals and foreign intelligence operations.

stories.Headline: IIT Jammu and NTT DATA launch an AI centre of excellence for research and startups
stories.Summary:
The Indian Institute of Technology Jammu and NTT DATA announced on 13 November 2026 a strategic collaboration to establish an Artificial Intelligence Centre of Excellence at IIT Jammu. NTT DATA is described as a global technology services provider and a global leader in digital business and technology services. The announcement was datelined Jammu, India, and dignitaries from both organisations exchanged MoU documents during a function in Jammu. Daily Excelsior reported the announcement on 14 November 2026, CASRAI published its editorial on 15 November 2026 and ETEducation published on 17 November 2026. The centre is intended to promote AI research, develop regional talent and address local challenges in Jammu and Kashmir.

The AI-CoE will focus on four areas: secure and responsible AI innovation, digital twins, physical AI, and research commercialisation and startup development. Secure and responsible AI covers small and large language models, agentic AI, AI governance and AI for Indian languages, with Dogri named as a target for making digital services more accessible. Potential applications include flood monitoring and early-warning systems for the Tawi and Chenab river basins and sensor-based approaches to landslide and flood risk. Physical AI combines AI with robotics, computer vision, IoT and edge computing for infrastructure monitoring, autonomous systems, situational awareness and public safety. A talent programme offers students, researchers and faculty industry projects, faculty engagement, fellowships, hackathons and hands-on training in AI, high-performance computing and edge computing.

NTT DATA will connect IIT Jammu's research capabilities with industry requirements through its global network of Innovation Centres. Avinash Joshi, Executive Managing Director for India at NTT DATA, said that AI's greatest impact happens when it helps solve real problems for people and communities. Professor Manoj Gaur, Director of IIT Jammu, said the aim is to create an environment where ideas can move from research to real-world application. Gaur said the collaboration will strengthen efforts towards research commercialisation, technology entrepreneurship and a strong deep-tech ecosystem in the region. Joshi and Gaur said the collaboration aims to translate research into practical solutions for regional challenges, with potential applications across India.

The announcement lists potential applications rather than committed projects, and adds that use cases elsewhere in the Jammu and Kashmir region are to be explored. Successful approaches could be adapted across India, and Gaur said innovations could have wider applications across India. Jammu and Kashmir's mountainous terrain and river systems present complex challenges related to floods, landslides, infrastructure planning and emergency response. The partnership will also support intellectual property development, product innovation and deep-tech startups in the region. Students, researchers and faculty are affected, along with deep-tech startups in Jammu and Kashmir and communities facing flood and landslide risks.

CASRAI describes the arrangement as an industry-hosted AI centre on a university campus combining research, student training and commercialisation. CASRAI notes that research offices weighing a similar arrangement typically need to settle the form of the sponsored research agreement, background and foreground IP, publication rights and data handling. The inclusion of AI governance in the stated scope connects to wider policy work such as India's AI governance guidelines and general principles of responsible AI. CASRAI states that membership-style models are another route to industry engagement, referring to its industry affiliates program entry. CASRAI adds that the stated emphasis on fellowships, hackathons and industry projects suggests student and faculty participation routes.

The announcement does not give financial terms, funding amounts, a duration or a governance structure for the centre. Questions such as who owns resulting intellectual property, how data is shared and how the centre will be staffed are not addressed in it. The announcement gives no eligibility rules or application process for the talent programme. CASRAI published its editorial reading of the announcement, not a statement from either organisation, and cites NTT DATA's announcement of 13 November 2026, checked 2026-11-15. CASRAI states that everything it publishes stays open to read, with no account and no card.

stories.Headline: Apple adds privacy controls in macOS 27.3 beta 2 to limit AI agents to user-approved apps and folders
stories.Summary:
Apple introduced new privacy controls for AI agents in macOS 27.3 beta 2 on November 17, 2026, to protect user data. These updates follow a period earlier this year when multiple AI agents went rogue and caused significant security concerns for users. Apple had previously informed developers in October that it would soon introduce stricter settings and clearer warnings for the operating system. The company wants to ensure that AI agents only have access to the specific apps or folders that users deem safe. These new guardrails are designed to help users understand the risks associated with granting full disk access to various apps.

The update splits the Device Control and Data Access API into Accessibility and System & App Protection Override for better clarity. Accessibility allows permissions for assistive tools through an entitlement process, while the other menu manages whether apps must seek permission. Users can now choose specific apps from a list or require an app to request permission every single time. For Full Disk Access, users can select exact folders for backup apps, disk cleaners, file indexers, or security apps. A transparency indicator will appear in the menu bar whenever an app controls another app using the protection override setting.

Apple stated in a developer blog post that granting extraordinary access puts all of the data on a Mac at risk. The company believes these changes empower users to make informed decisions about their own personal data and their overall privacy. Apple expects developers to adjust how their apps request permissions to handle access to only a limited set of folders. Developers should ensure their apps gracefully handle these limited permissions when utilizing the affected APIs to maintain a good experience. Apple noted that additional details regarding the new entitlements for developers would be made available to them very soon.

MacRumors reported that Apple raised concerns about developers using permissions in ways that could put sensitive user data at risk. Granting full disk access could expose personal files, emails, messages, and browsing history to AI agents that might behave unpredictably. Users of Mac computers, especially the Studio and the mini, are affected as these machines became popular for local AI. These users are now given more visibility into the data that apps can access or control when given full permissions. The new controls alert users to risks without removing the ability to grant system wide access if they choose.

Mac computers became popular for running AI models locally, leading to a surge in demand for the Studio and mini. Apple was short on supply earlier this year due to this unexpected trend in how people used their hardware. Former CEO Tim Cook mentioned in May that the company was surprised by the high demand for these specific machines. Permissions that users granted before the release of macOS 27.3 will remain in effect without any immediate changes. Currently known apps will retain their existing experience without needing an entitlement to function as they did before.

Developers of assistive technologies or backup apps can request entitlements to offer the same experience for new installations as before. The new revised options will only appear to users when they are approving new app permission requests for software. Apple has not specified exactly when these beta features will move to a final, stable release for all Mac users. The articles leave open how many developers will successfully implement the graceful handling of limited folder and app access. It remains unclear if these granular controls will fully prevent AI agents from going rogue in the future.

stories.Headline: Google launches AlloyDB Express to provide fast database provisioning for developers and AI coding agents
stories.Summary:
Google launched AlloyDB Express in preview on November 18, 2026, for developers and AI coding agents. This new version of AlloyDB for PostgreSQL addresses database bottlenecks for software teams using AI tools. The service allows for the creation of a PostgreSQL database in under two seconds. Users can provision these databases through the gcloud CLI, REST API, MCP, Terraform, or the Google Cloud console. The system pauses automatically after 15 minutes of inactivity and resumes when a new query arrives.

The service targets engineering teams needing fast provisioning for prototypes, internal applications, and testing while maintaining central security controls. Administrators can centrally set identity, network, and organisation policies that apply automatically to databases created by users or agents. Security features include public DNS endpoints that mask IP addresses and block incoming traffic unless it is explicitly allowed. Internal workloads connect through private DNS or Private Service Connect, with access managed by Google Cloud IAM and VPC Service Controls. Native PostgreSQL roles also manage access controls for these isolated environments.

Google stated that the service combines traditional transactional workloads with search, retrieval, and model-linked functions for AI application development. They built AI features directly into the service, removing the need for external tooling or a separate vector database. The company provides natural language-to-SQL generation through AlloyDB Studio and related APIs for developers and AI agents. Users can access Gemini models inside SQL queries to run semantic filtering, ranking, summarisation, and generate embeddings. The service supports vector search using Google's ScaNN index and pgvector HNSW to store vector embeddings.

Engineering teams and AI agents are affected by this shift toward balancing AI speed with infrastructure and data access controls. Other reports show threat actors using AI agents for live intrusions, including a multi-agent framework called exploit_agent. The FBI issued a FLASH alert on November 13 regarding the ARTEX framework used against government and financial sectors. Other tools like CAIRN, CyberStrikeAI, PentAGI, and HexStrike AI are being used by financially motivated actors and China-nexus espionage outfits. These attackers can find and exploit vulnerabilities and change tactics based on the target's response.

The background shows a paradigm shift where intrusions occur at machine speed through the automated chaining of complex attack paths. Google Threat Intelligence Group found that disclosures and exploits nearly doubled between January and August 2026. Zero-day exploits jumped to 22 in August 2026, compared to a 2025 average of 8 per month. Mandiant responded to LLMJacking incidents in 2026 where attackers burned through compute quotas, with some fraudulent charges reaching $1 million. North Korean actors used AI to create fake recruiter profiles and deploy the SOMBERMEME backdoor.

AlloyDB Express uses consumption-based pricing with active compute at USD $0.115 per Compute Unit hour and storage at USD $0.30 per GB-month. Google offers a free tier with 50 free Compute Units each month and charges USD $0.00 for paused compute. Customers can upgrade to full AlloyDB with one click, keeping data, schemas, users, and connection strings unchanged. This upgrade provides access to disaster recovery features, read replicas, and high availability for production applications. The articles leave open how defenders will counter the increasing stealth and sophistication of AI-driven attacks.

stories.Headline: Apple limits advanced Siri AI requests in iOS 27.3 and ties higher limits to iCloud+ plans
stories.Summary:
Apple revealed earlier this week that Siri AI usage limits will be implemented in iOS 27.3, and 9to5Mac reported on November 18, 2026, that a real-world example of hitting the limits had appeared. In the iOS 27.3 beta, Ben posted on X that he hit his Siri AI daily usage limit, and that Siri still worked, including complex questions. In a follow-up post, Ben clarified that complex questions did stop working shortly after he posted. Basic requests continued to work as usual, because they do not have a usage limit. Apple explained how iCloud+ increases those limits, according to 9to5Mac.

Siri AI and select other AI features will begin having usage limits in iOS 27.3 for advanced tasks. Apple shares just two examples of something advanced, including the request to text Mark the address for Annika's party and tell him what time to leave from home to make it on time. Leaker pdfu posted on X the instructions Siri AI follows to decide whether a request is basic or advanced. A request is advanced if it uses information from one app, from what is on screen or from a message, in a different app, or needs a result from one step used in a different step or app. A request is also advanced if it contains two or more separate asks in one sentence, even in the same app, though extra details of one action, such as a cc or a time, are still one ask.

Apple is responsible for the limits, and the company has not made clear what qualifies as a complex or advanced Siri AI request. Apple shares just two examples of something advanced, and 9to5Mac said it would be helpful if Apple publicly documented these guidelines for users. 9to5Mac suggested that perhaps after iOS 27.3 ships and usage limits are fully implemented, more detail will come from the company. 9to5Mac asked readers what they think of Siri AI's parameters for advanced requests in iOS 27.3.

According to pdfu's list, a request is advanced if it asks about or summarizes the content of a photo, a camera view or an attachment, while editing, searching and albums are fine. A request is advanced if it deletes, archives, junks, moves, marks or changes a set, meaning all, every, these or a whole category, of the user's emails, notes, reminders, messages, photos, files, contacts or events. A request is advanced if it sets a device action or a notification to run on a time or trigger, not alarms, timers, reminders or calendar events, or notifies someone when a person arrives or leaves, or builds or edits a Shortcut or automation. A request is advanced if it asks Siri to compose or create new content, such as a story, poem, essay, plan, recipe, image, or an email or message from a topic rather than wording the user gives, or to rewrite in a tone other than friendly, professional or concise. Siri AI checks the request against this list, and if it involves any of these, it is deemed advanced.

9to5Mac said the limits are standard practice with other AI services like ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude, because these tools rely on server-based models rather than running entirely on-device. Cult of Mac reported on November 17, 2026, that Siri AI usage limits will depend on your iCloud+ plan. 9to5Mac reported that Apple revealed the limits and explained how iCloud+ increases them. The iOS 27.3 beta provided the example of Ben hitting his daily limit. Ben's follow-up clarified that complex questions stopped working shortly after his first post.

9to5Mac said that perhaps after iOS 27.3 ships and usage limits are fully implemented, we will get more detail from Apple. 9to5Mac left open what qualifies as a complex or advanced Siri AI request, because Apple has not made that clear. 9to5Mac also left open whether Apple will publicly document the guidelines for users. 9to5Mac asked readers what they think of the parameters for advanced requests in iOS 27.3. Cult of Mac's report was headlined around iCloud+ plans, and 9to5Mac's report was headlined around what counts toward the limit.
