stories.Headline: Fireworks AI CEO Lin Qiao sets out a framework for AI data retention
stories.Summary:
A November 13, 2026 post on X by Fireworks AI cofounder and CEO Lin Qiao set out a framework for understanding AI data retention, and MarkTechPost explained it on November 17, 2026 by describing two standard API designs that decide where control of the data lifecycle sits. In the first design, a customer uploads a file or dataset, runs jobs against it, and then deletes it, with the platform keeping the data stored and available until deletion is requested. In the second design, a customer sends data, the platform computes and returns a result, and no application state stays behind, which is the pattern called zero data retention. The article says data retention has become one of the most misunderstood terms in AI infrastructure, and that after a wave of AI security headlines many development teams now ask whether their AI provider keeps their data.

The article describes zero data retention as a per-endpoint commitment not to persist covered prompts and outputs after an eligible request, with eligibility depending on the endpoint, request flags and account settings rather than the vendor name. It says stored features such as batch, file and dataset features keep data until it is deleted or expires, and it advises preferring ephemeral endpoints because deletion is the customer's job after an upload. Among the examples it gives, OpenAI Batch requires uploading a JSONL input file and then creating the batch, Amazon Bedrock batch inference keeps input JSONL files in an S3 location the customer chooses, the Gemini Batch API runs jobs from an input file the customer provides, and Fireworks AI Batch requires creating a dataset and then submitting jobs against it. The article says OpenAI batch files last 30 days by default and Anthropic batch data 29 days, that OpenAI non-batch files persist until deleted, and that Fireworks AI managed training datasets have no time limit and are deleted by the customer, while Amazon Bedrock and Google batch jobs read and write the customer's own cloud storage.

On the ephemeral side, the article lists OpenAI Chat Completions, where store defaults to false, Amazon Bedrock Converse, where content is only used to generate the response, and Google Gemini text generation, which is stateless when store is false. It also lists Fireworks AI Chat Completions, direct or through Nexus, whose schema has no store field, and the Fireworks AI Training SDK including Serverless Training, where forward_backward sends tokenized batches per call, no dataset is uploaded, and training data is not stored at rest. The article says a synchronous response alone does not establish zero data retention, and it cites OpenAI's data controls as describing two layers, application state that a feature must keep, such as uploaded files, and abuse-monitoring logs held for safety review, noting that a platform can be at zero on one layer and not the other. According to the article, Qiao said Fireworks AI keeps nothing after a deletion request, and the article adds that the same split has shaped data processing systems for decades.

Articles.Title: Clearing Up the Confusion on AI Data Retention: Two Standard Designs Explained

stories.headline_source: Clearing Up the Confusion on AI Data Retention: Two Standard Designs Explained

stories.Headline: Perplexity adds Multiagent feature to allow up to 16 AI agents to cross-check complex tasks
stories.Summary:
Perplexity added a feature called Multiagent to its Computer research platform on November 17, 2026. This new system allows a lead agent to manage a team of up to 16 supporting agents to complete complex tasks. These agents work in parallel, share findings directly with one another, and cross-check each other's work. The lead agent plans the overall task, assigns specific parts to the team, and merges all findings into one final response for the user.

This update introduces the highest effort level available, sitting above the Ultra setting. It requires a Perplexity Max plan, which costs 167 dollars per month when billed annually, and is available only on the web. The default team utilizes three model families, specifically Claude Opus 5.5, GPT 6.1 Sol, and Gemini 4 Carbon. Users can name specific models in their queries, and the system allows agents to coordinate edits within shared files.

Perplexity stated that this tool is designed for large, interconnected work such as annual report reviews and year-end tax preparation. The company explained that the lead agent acts as the single point of contact for the user while coordinating the supporting agents. This builds upon effort controls launched on September 17, 2026, which previously offered Light, Standard, High, and Ultra settings. The company positions this diversity of models as a key difference from competitors like Kimi and Grok.

Articles.Title: Perplexity Computer Adds Multiagent: Up to 16 AI Agents That Cross-Check Work

stories.Headline: HCLTech and Cohere partner to build sovereign AI solutions for enterprises and governments
stories.Summary:
HCLTech and Cohere announced on 17 November 2026 that they have partnered to build and deliver sovereign artificial intelligence solutions for enterprises and governments. Under the agreement, HCLTech will become one of Cohere's preferred global systems integrator partners in Canada and Germany. The two companies plan to combine Cohere's sovereign AI platform and models with HCLTech's professional services and AI implementation capabilities. They also intend to extend the partnership to other markets beyond Canada and Germany. The initial development work will focus on insurance, financial services, and manufacturing, according to the companies.

Potential applications include jurisdiction-aware claims assessment, secure analysis of sensitive financial data, and faster access to technical documentation. The partnership will use Cohere's models and its North agentic AI platform, alongside domain-adapted models and retrieval and reasoning capabilities. The companies said the solutions would be deployed in customers' preferred environments to address data residency, security, and regulatory requirements. Phil Blunsom, Chief Technology Officer at Cohere, said organisations should not have to choose between the benefits of AI and control over their data. He said the partnership with HCLTech would help customers tackle complex, industry-specific challenges while meeting their security, governance and data sovereignty requirements.

HCLTech Executive Vice President and Canada Country Head Dave Chopra said the partnership would combine Cohere's platform with HCLTech's local presence in Canada to help organisations adopt AI. The companies also said both hold ISO 42001 certification, the international standard for AI management systems. Cohere was co-founded by Aidan Gomez, Nick Frosst, and Ivan Zhang in 2019, and Gomez was the youngest co-author of the landmark Google research paper that invented the Transformer architecture powering generative AI. The agreement follows HCLTech's October partnership with Anthropic to expand enterprise adoption of agentic AI through its Claude models, which included plans for a dedicated Anthropic business unit and a Centre of Excellence. HCLTech has also pursued sovereign AI initiatives in India, and in February HCLSoftware partnered with Sify Digital Services to develop a sovereign AI stack for Indian enterprises.

Articles.Title: HCLTech Partners With Transformer Co-Author-Led Cohere to Target Sovereign AI Markets - Analytics India Magazine

stories.Headline: Accenture LearnVantage and Google Cloud partner to expand AI education across over 1,000 Indian schools and colleges
stories.Summary:
Accenture LearnVantage and Google Cloud announced on 17 November 2026 that they will partner to expand AI education across more than 1,000 public and private schools and colleges in India, combining hands-on learning programmes with industry-aligned certifications. The initiative will pair Accenture LearnVantage's learning programmes with Google Cloud's unified AI stack to set up AI Labs in schools and Centres of Excellence in higher education institutions. The programmes will cover foundational AI literacy, applied generative AI, agentic AI and AI engineering, with the stated aim of preparing students for emerging technology roles. The partnership will also introduce structured learning pathways for students and educators, supported by Google's AI tools and personalised coaching through Gemini.

At the school level, the two companies plan to establish AI Labs powered by Google Gemini that introduce younger students to foundational AI concepts in controlled learning environments where they can experiment with AI tools and develop practical skills. For higher education institutions, the partnership plans Centres of Excellence, centres and academies that will serve as hubs for applied learning, innovation and industry collaboration, giving students access to modern tools, expert mentorship and opportunities to work with emerging technologies. The curriculum will include generative AI and agentic AI literacy, applied generative AI and agentic AI programmes, an AI developer programme and AI engineering, and students who complete the programmes and assessments will receive certifications. The platform will also offer guided learning pathways, multilingual voice capabilities and AI-driven content to make learning more accessible, and institutions will be able to explore customised offerings, including degree programmes, aligned with changing industry requirements.

Anurag Bansal, Managing Director of Accenture LearnVantage for Asia Oceania and the Middle East, said in a statement that the future of learning will be shaped by how learning pathways and talent creation for careers are reimagined as those careers continue to evolve. The collaboration will also support Accenture LearnVantage's existing national AI initiatives, including the National AI Olympiad and AI Infinity, which aim to encourage AI literacy and introduce students to careers in emerging technologies. The announcement was published by Analytics India Magazine on 17 November 2026, the same day the outlet listed a related story on HCLTech partnering with Cohere to target sovereign AI markets. The articles do not say what funding the initiative involves, how institutions will be selected or when the labs and centres are expected to open.

stories.Headline: Dreamteam raises $53m to build AI-native CRM with four AI sales teammates
stories.Summary:
Dreamteam has raised $53 million across its seed and Series A rounds to build an AI-native customer relationship management platform that uses multiple AI teammates to manage sales workflows and customer relationships. The funding was led by Together Fund and Accel, with participation from Premji Invest, according to an article published by Analytics India Magazine on 17 November 2026. The company says more than 100 companies across 13 countries currently use its platform. The money will help Dreamteam expand the platform, which aims to reduce the manual work involved in maintaining traditional CRM systems. The platform currently offers four AI teammates, each assigned a specific sales function.

Rachel acts as a market analyst who researches prospects and their companies, while Sally manages deals and follow-ups. Raj monitors sales pipelines and identifies potential risks, and Alex handles CRM configuration based on business requirements. The four agents operate through a shared system called Company Brain, which keeps customer information from calls, emails and meetings, so the agents can access previous conversations, customer priorities and outstanding commitments instead of working independently. The system is also designed to update CRM records as customer relationships and business requirements change. Anand Venkatraman, co-founder and CEO of Dreamteam, said AI finally gives the company a way to change the foundation of CRM.

He said Dreamteam learns from the work a team is already doing, keeps the context alive and gives every salesperson skilled AI teammates that can reason over it and move work forward. Dreamteam argues that conventional CRMs, where representatives manually record interactions, update deal information and track follow-ups, often fail to capture important details from customer conversations. The company says its agents operate within company-defined policies, pricing rules and approval limits, that emails require human approval before being sent, and that users can inspect the sources behind recommendations and correct information stored by the system. Dreamteam plans to expand the agents' responsibilities beyond individual sales tasks to manage broader customer journeys, including lead generation, renewals and account expansion. It also envisions its agents eventually communicating with buyers' AI systems to exchange requirements and handle routine business interactions.

stories.Headline: UNESCO publishes a teaching guide to help educators teach critical thinking about AI-generated information
stories.Summary:
UNESCO published a teaching guide on 17 November 2026 to help educators prepare learners to question AI-generated information and understand how automated systems shape what people encounter online. The publication, titled AI Answers. You Decide. ,  Teaching Media and Information Literacy in AI-Mediated Information Environments, offers discussion questions, activities and examples for educators, teacher-training institutions and curriculum developers. It extends UNESCO's existing media and information literacy curriculum to address an information environment increasingly influenced by AI.

The guide addresses the reliability and authenticity of AI-generated content alongside questions about the systems, interests and data behind it. The guide's scope includes convincing synthetic text, images, audio and video, as well as the algorithms that influence which information people see. Five connected areas organize the material: AI in everyday life, AI and the media, AI, the human mind and knowledge, AI, power and human rights, and AI and the future. The knowledge strand focuses on critical thinking, informed trust and evaluating AI-generated information, while the media strand examines changes to journalism, content creation and access to information.

Questions about power and human rights bring algorithmic bias, inequality and sustainability into the curriculum, and the future-focused material encourages learners to participate in shaping inclusive, human-centered approaches to AI. The publication is a companion to UNESCO's Media and Information Literate Citizens: Think Critically, Click Wisely! curriculum, launched in 2021 and subsequently piloted and adapted in more than 40 countries. The new guide was developed with eight international experts and peer-reviewed by ten additional specialists.

Mariya Gabriel, Assistant-Director General for Communication and Information at UNESCO, said artificial intelligence is transforming how people learn, communicate and access information, and that people must retain the ability to think critically, question what they see and make informed choices. Anne Leppäjärvi, who authored the guide, said AI does not change the foundations of media and information literacy but the environment in which they are applied, and that the goal is to equip learners with critical thinking skills rather than keep up with every technological change. Educators can adapt the guide's conceptual explanations, discussion questions, practical activities and examples to their own educational settings. The articles do not say what happens next beyond that, and they give no further dates or plans for the guide's rollout.

Articles.Title: UNESCO releases AI media literacy teaching guide to strengthen critical thinking - EdTech Innovation Hub

stories.headline_source: UNESCO releases AI media literacy teaching guide to strengthen critical thinking

stories.Headline: CtrlS Datacentres targets 4.4 GW of data centre capacity by 2030
stories.Summary:
CtrlS Datacentres is targeting 4.4 GW of data centre capacity by 2030, the company said in an interview published by Analytics India Magazine on 16 November 2026. Rahul Dhar, President of Global Data Centre Operations, Enterprise Colo Delivery, Programme Management and Energy R&D at CtrlS Datacentres, gave the interview to AIM. CtrlS recently announced a ₹10,000 crore investment in Bihar to set up a 150 MW AI factory in Bodh Gaya. The company is also expanding its presence in Bihar with a ₹400 crore data centre in Patna. CtrlS’s Patna data centre currently has 12 MW of IT capacity, with scope to scale up as demand increases.

The strategy is to bring infrastructure closer to customers, particularly content-based businesses that need to serve users in smaller cities, Dhar said. Dhar said the new facility would support demand for digital infrastructure in Bihar and eastern India. CtrlS plans to establish more than 20 edge data centres across tier-2 and tier-3 cities over the coming years with improved fibre connectivity. It currently operates 19 data centres across 10 cities, including Lucknow, Noida, Kolkata and Gandhinagar, and operates a containerised data centre in Bhubaneswar. Hyperscalers constitute the largest source of demand for CtrlS, although the company also serves nearly 40 Indian public and private sector banks.

Nikhil Kamath, Co-founder of Zerodha, and entrepreneur Sreeram Reddy Vanga recently invested a combined ₹250 crore in CtrlS Datacenters. Canadian Pension Plan Investment Board also invested around ₹7,000 crore in the company earlier this year. Dhar attributes investor interest in CtrlS to its focus on hyperscale campuses, advance planning for high-capacity grid power, and modular designs. CtrlS is building greenfield data centre campuses for hyperscalers in Hyderabad and Mumbai. It is also in discussions with neocloud companies seeking capacity, and expects to deliver against its existing commitments over the next 12, 24 months.

This year, the central government introduced a 21-year tax holiday for foreign companies providing global cloud services using India-based data centres. Dhar said it won’t affect CtrlS’s existing demand, which is driven by domestic customers as well as global technology companies. He said that even with the tax holiday and a possible influx of foreign investors, Indian colocation providers have a good order book in hand. Dhar said India needs to shorten the period for forecasting data centre power requirements and speed up approvals for power transmission lines and fibre networks. Utilities and government departments typically seek power consumption on 7, 8 year horizons, he said.

Dhar said the projection that typical governments or power or utility departments ask for can be reduced to three to four years. Data centres are growing from facilities with capacities of around 5, 8 megawatts to campuses ranging from 10, 100 MW. Dhar said operators are bulk consumers of power, so they need better planning or better awareness among various government departments on how much power they need, at what time and at which location. He also called for faster right-of-way approvals to lay fibre networks and transmission lines, particularly when operators acquire land on city outskirts. CtrlS is providing inputs to government bodies and industry associations, including the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, NASSCOM and the Confederation of Indian Industry, on India’s recently proposed data centre policy.

Several states, including Telangana, Uttar Pradesh, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Maharashtra, have already introduced data centre policies. According to Mordor Intelligence estimates, India consumed about 150 billion litres of water in 2025 to cool about 1.5 GW of data centre capacity, a figure expected to more than double by 2030. CtrlS uses closed-loop chillers to limit water loss and is reusing treated wastewater at one of its Mumbai facilities to reduce dependence on fresh water. The company also owns and operates a nearly 100 MW captive solar farm in Nagpur, with the power fed into the grid to offset consumption at its Mumbai data centres and similar initiatives planned for other locations, including Hyderabad. CtrlS also operates its facilities at a power usage effectiveness of around 1.4.

Dhar said CtrlS is prepared to support customers deploying liquid-cooled infrastructure, including GPU providers and cloud companies. He said all of CtrlS’s data centres are rated tier-4 data centres, and the company uses external certification and has introduced an Integrated Command and Control Centre in Hyderabad to monitor infrastructure centrally. The centre supports predictive analysis and preventive maintenance, and CtrlS is also applying AI to infrastructure monitoring, including CCTV systems, to improve responses to operational issues. Dhar said data centre operators will need to keep adapting their facilities to changing chip technologies, power densities and cooling systems as AI workloads increase infrastructure requirements. The article was published on 16 November 2026.

stories.Headline: Sarvam AI launches Token Factory inference engine to provide enterprises with local model access in India
stories.Summary:
Sarvam AI launched its Token Factory inference engine on November 18, 2026, to provide enterprises with local AI model access. This new offering allows users to run workloads on GPUs located in India through a single API. The unicorn aims to capture the local inference market by offering high speeds and low latency. It uses a three-tier caching architecture to rival the performance of global inference leaders. The company targets enterprises that must follow strict data residency mandates for their sensitive information.

Token Factory hosts Sarvam's 105B model and open-weight models from Google, DeepSeek, GLM, and Kimi in India. BFSI customers can access dedicated GPU capacity and on-premises inference deployments to ensure their data remains secure. Other providers like Krutrim have hosted DeepSeek models since last year, and OpenAI offers GPT-6 Luna workloads. Anthropic provides in-country inference for select Claude models through Amazon Bedrock to compete in the region. These diverse options create a crowded arena for any company offering local AI inference services.

Sarvam claims that hosting global models on Indian infrastructure supports data residency for local enterprises. The company believes that clients will pay for multi-model flexibility and the security of sovereign infrastructure. However, critics argue that relying on foreign open-weight models might dilute the push for homegrown AI. They question if the company can truly champion sovereign Indian AI while hosting overseas models. Sarvam must now invest in GPUs and software to maintain its competitive edge against giants.

Global AI giants like OpenAI and Anthropic have opened offices in India to ramp up local investments. Anthropic saw a 15X increase in Indian downloads from July to September, while ChatGPT downloads fell 21%. Despite this, OpenAI revenue from in-app purchases in India grew 70% during the third quarter of 2026. The broader AI ecosystem is expected to contribute 1.7 trillion dollars to India's GDP by 2035. These trends show that India has become a major battleground for the world's leading AI companies.

Perplexity CEO Aravind Srinivas now plans to file for a US IPO by the first quarter of 2027. He previously stated the company would not go public before 2028, but growth has exceeded his expectations. Perplexity reached an annual recurring revenue of 1 billion dollars, beating its previous projection of 750 million. Meanwhile, Anthropic is set to list on the Nasdaq this week, and OpenAI has filed confidentially. These moves indicate a broader trend of major AI firms seeking public listings in the US.

The articles leave open whether Sarvam can outpace global giants or if its playbook arrived too late. It remains unclear if the company can successfully woo enough clients to justify its GPU investments. The future of the Indian AI market depends on how enterprises balance sovereign needs with global model power. Other stories mention a grooming brand called H.I.M. and Urban Company's 2,500 crore rupee placement. FirstCry and Lorazzo also face various growth targets and market opportunities through the coming years.

stories.Headline: Google rolls out Tasks AI assistant to users in India with Gemini 4 Hydrogen
stories.Summary:
Google has begun rolling out its new agentic AI assistant Tasks, formerly Gemini Sparks, to users in India, the company announced in a blogpost. Josh Woodward, the vice-president of Google Labs and the Gemini app, wrote the post announcing the rollout. The service comes bundled for free with Google's new Gemini 4 Hydrogen model. Woodward said the update is rolling out free of charge for hundreds of millions of people across the US, Japan, Korea, Canada, Australia, and India. Tasks was reportedly initially launched to select testers back in May as Gemini Spark, an agentic AI helper.

The new feature will enable users to assign tasks to the AI assistant, including making calls, booking appointments, comparing products, making payments and completing purchases. Gemini can draw on information already available within Google services, including Gmail, Calendar, Maps, Photos, files and payment cards, to carry out tasks on a user's behalf. With Tasks, Gemini can call businesses, wait through hold periods, identify available appointment slots and add bookings to a user's calendar. Under the hood, Gemini uses the agent payments protocol (AP2) to enable Tasks to make purchases online. Google said it plans to integrate the universal commerce protocol (UCP) into Gemini to further streamline the checkout experience.

Woodward said the update is rolling out free of charge across the six markets using the Gemini 4 Hydrogen model. Google said it is working with American Express, Mastercard and Visa to enable tokenised card transactions via Tasks. However, the big tech juggernaut did not specify whether partnerships extend to India too. Google has also invited app developers to join its Connected Apps Platform, which could pave the way for Indian consumer, fintech, travel tech and foodtech brands to build task-based third-party integrations with the assistant. Unlike Gemini's Chat that only generates responses to a user's queries, Tasks goes one step further and enables the chatbot to perform basic functions.

India's inclusion in the initial rollout gives Google a large market to test consumer adoption of the personal AI assistant feature. Adoption will depend on the availability of supported merchants, payment methods and third-party apps in the country, and there appears to be no clarity on this front. These features could make Gemini Tasks a channel for online shopping, bill payments and routine purchases. The launch is part of a broader wave of big tech giants rolling out personal AI assistants to capture the masses.

In September, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg showcased the company's new offering called Muse, which allows an AI agent to send emails, fill forms, make plans and even make purchases autonomously. Prior to this, OpenAI also introduced Dots that can draft board meeting decks, conduct background research, and handle multi-step project management. xAI has also been developing Grok Bot, which sees cleaning up sales records and processing invoices as potential uses for agents. Microsoft is also pursuing agents, built on OpenClaw, which can function as digital teammates.

Back home, Emergent, better known for its vibe-coding platform, launched Wingman, an autonomous agent that handles routine actions and seeks approval before taking bigger steps. Tasks was subsequently expanded to the US-based subscribers of the Google AI Ultra tier. With the rollout, Google could be looking to expand the role of AI assistants beyond answering questions to embedding them in daily life. Google is now rolling out this feature for free in six markets.

To further scale the rollout, Google has invited app developers to join its Connected Apps Platform. The articles leave open whether the card partnerships with American Express, Mastercard and Visa extend to India. The articles also leave open the availability of supported merchants, payment methods and third-party apps in the country. More to follow.

stories.Headline: Dreamteam raises $53 Mn to build an AI-native CRM platform
stories.Summary:
Dreamteam, an AI-native customer relationship management platform cofounded by former Freshworks executives, emerged out of stealth mode and raised $53 Mn, nearly ₹498 Cr, in a strategic funding round from Together Fund, Accel and Premji Invest, as reported by Inc42 on November 16, 2026. The startup did not elaborate how it plans to utilise the funds. Founded in 2025 by former Freshworks executives Anand Venkatraman, Ramesh Parthasarathy and Senthil Kanthaswamy, Dreamteam is building an AI-powered CRM platform. Its four AI agents help enterprises track commitments, flag pipeline risks and automate routine sales workflows. The startup claims its AI platform pulls data and context from customer conversations, emails and Zoom interactions to enable AI coworkers to automate regular work.

Dreamteam claims to already cater to hundreds of companies across industries such as AI, online media, healthcare, manufacturing and consulting. The platform also allows businesses to create custom apps and dashboards using natural language without writing code. Going forward, Dreamteam said it plans to focus on expanding its use cases across the entire customer lifecycle, including prospecting, onboarding and upselling. The fundraise comes amid growing investor interest in Indian AI startups. As per Inc42 data, homegrown AI ventures raised $438 Mn across 35 deals in Q2 2026, up 265% year on year.

Together Fund cofounder and partner Girish Mathrubootham said CRM is among the biggest software categories ripe for disruption. He said he had worked alongside Dreamteam's founders since day one as their vision for an AI-native CRM took shape. He said their deep CRM expertise and proven record of scaling enterprise software make them uniquely positioned to lead this reinvention. Venture capital and private equity firms remain bullish on startups that help enterprises put AI to work across business functions. Just last month, US-based AI code testing startup Blacksmith bagged $66 Mn in its Series C round led by Sequoia Capital.

Prior to this in October itself, another enterprise AI startup AuxoAI raised $20.7 Mn in its Series A funding round led by NTTVC. Fractal Analytics CEO Srikanth Velamakanni also recently reportedly said the AI analytics company is in discussions with 20-25 AI startups for potential acquisitions. At the heart of all this is the growing Indian enterprise AI ecosystem, which is projected to become a $71 Bn opportunity by 2030. The articles do not say when the round closed or what valuation it gave Dreamteam. More to follow.

stories.Headline: Reliance Jio stops new claims for its free Google AI Pro subscription
stories.Summary:
Reliance Jio has stopped accepting new claims for its free Google AI Pro subscription, which gave eligible users up to 18 months of access to Google's premium Gemini features. The redemption window ran from October 30, 2025, to October 29, 2026, according to terms and conditions listed on Jio's website. Jio's support page now says the offer is unavailable on new recharges or plan upgrades. The offer initially covered users over the age of 18 on unlimited 5G plans priced at ₹349 or above. Starting February 11, 2026, Jio temporarily extended eligibility to users on plans priced at ₹299 or above that offered 1.5 GB of data per day.

Users who activated the offer can continue using the subscription for up to 18 months from activation, provided they maintain an eligible recharge plan. Eligible users could activate the subscription, valued at ₹1,950 per month, through the MyJio app. Subscribers were required to maintain an eligible recharge plan throughout the subscription period to retain access to the benefits. Jio reserved the right to suspend access if users failed to maintain the required plan. The development comes a year after Reliance Industries Ltd, through its AI arm Reliance Intelligence, partnered with Google to accelerate AI adoption in India by offering free Google AI Pro access to Jio users.

Announcing the partnership, RIL said the 18-month subscription would provide access to Gemini 2.5 Pro through the Gemini app, higher limits for image and video generation using Nano Banana and Veo models, expanded access to NotebookLM, and 2 TB of cloud storage, among other benefits. The company valued the combined package at ₹35,100 per user. Beyond the consumer-facing offering, the partnership also positioned Reliance Intelligence as a strategic Google Cloud partner in India, with plans to expand access to Google's proprietary AI hardware accelerators, or TPUs, for local organisations. Inc42 has reached out to Jio for further details on the development, and the story will be updated on receiving a response. Separately, Jio Platforms is in talks with the Indian Space Research Organisation, Skyroot Aerospace, and other domestic launch providers for its proposed constellation of 1,600 satellites in low Earth orbit.

The company is exploring whether it can carry out the programme in India, from satellite design to launch and operations. It is also in discussions with SpaceX. Jio Platforms listed on the BSE and NSE on October 28 at ₹1,358 apiece, a 21.4% premium to its issue price of ₹1,119. On the financial front, the company reported a net profit of ₹8,387 Cr in Q2 FY27, marking a 13.7% increase from ₹7,379 Cr in the year-ago quarter. Sequentially, net profit grew 8% from ₹7,764 Cr in Q1 FY27.

Operating revenue rose 11.4% YoY and 3.3% sequentially to ₹40,475 Cr in the quarter under review. The offer was the consumer-facing part of Reliance's AI partnership with Google, which also covers the distribution of Gemini Enterprise and access to Google's AI chips for Indian organisations. The redemption window ended on October 29, 2026, a year after the offer launched. Eligible subscribers could activate the offer through the MyJio app. More to follow.

stories.Headline: Inc42 identifies five emerging AI startups focusing on infrastructure and autonomy
stories.Summary:
Inc42 published a curated list of five emerging AI startups in November 2026. The editorial team selected these companies for their focus on infrastructure, autonomy, and measurement. These startups build tools for inference routing, semantic video intelligence, autonomous commerce, AI-native CRM, and pipeline generation. They aim to help enterprises run AI models more efficiently, reliably, and at scale. The list is not a ranking and is presented in alphabetical order.

BLUE, founded in 2023 in Bengaluru, uses a codec to cut storage by 90 percent. Kily was founded in March 2025 in Bengaluru by Sankalp Mehrotra, Anurag Singh, and Sharad Chitlangia. Revspot, founded in 2024 in Bengaluru, raised 4.8 million dollars in a Series A round. RouterPlus was founded in 2026 by Alok Bishoyi and Lakshmi Narayana for LLM routing. Superleap, founded in 2024 in Bengaluru, was started by Subham Kumar Boundia, Alok Maurya, and Saurabh Maheshwari.

Kunal Kislay leads BLUE, which turns CCTV feeds into a searchable intelligence layer for enterprises. Kily uses Core Decision AI to manage marketplace listings and pricing for over 50 brands. Revspot created Spot, an AI growth agent that generates qualified pipelines for high-ticket B2C businesses. RouterPlus matches requests to models like Claude, GPT, Gemini, Qwen, and DeepSeek using customer evals. Superleap uses SuperOS, SuperSense, and SuperAgents to rebuild the CRM category as a revenue operating system.

Britannia and Hindustan Petroleum use BLUE, while Kily works with ITC, Unilever, Mondelez, and Coca-Cola. Revspot serves over 50 customers in real estate, education, automotive, and wealth management sectors. RouterPlus helps teams manage API keys and contracts while shifting from closed to open-source models. Superleap counts Razorpay, Aakash Education, Cars24, and MediBuddy as customers for its AI-native revenue system. These tools affect businesses struggling with the trade-off between intelligence, speed, performance, and cost.

Indian boardrooms previously focused on which large language model to adopt for their enterprise needs. Now, the priority has shifted toward the cost of running these models and inference spending. Recent funding includes 20.7 million dollars for AuxoAI, 66 million dollars for Blacksmith, and 2.3 million dollars for QwikBuild. Spill Games also raised 10.5 million dollars for AI-led mobile gaming in late October. Investors are now betting on companies that deploy existing models rather than new frontier models.

The global video analytics market is projected to reach 33.61 billion dollars by 2031. The AI sales agent market is estimated at 3.4 billion dollars in 2026 and 15.8 billion by 2033. The AI model router market is estimated at 100 million dollars in 2025 and 4.1 billion by 2035. The global CRM market is projected to reach about 321 billion dollars by 2034. The articles leave open how these specific startups will scale within these growing global markets.

stories.Headline: KiteFishAI launches NanoI1 open-weight model for specialised AI applications
stories.Summary:
KiteFishAI, an Indian artificial intelligence startup, launched a compact open-weight AI model called NanoI1 on November 18, 2026, according to a TechGig report published that morning. The company said the model is designed for developers, startups and enterprises that are building specialised AI applications with a strong focus on data security and deployment requirements. KiteFishAI described NanoI1 as a foundational element for purpose-built AI solutions rather than a direct competitor to large language models built for a wide range of general tasks. The official announcement did not include detailed benchmark results, specific model parameters, pricing information or hardware requirements for the new model.

The launch is meant to make AI adoption more accessible for businesses that need solutions tailored precisely to their own operational needs, including organisations in highly regulated industries where data security, compliance and deployment demands are paramount. According to KiteFishAI, smaller purpose-built models offer a practical alternative to relying on large general-purpose models for every application, and they give organisations greater control over their AI deployments. The company also said compact models enable applications built around specific business requirements, which fosters enhanced customisation and operational alignment. With NanoI1, KiteFishAI is looking to contribute to India's rapidly expanding AI development ecosystem by giving developers and businesses an accessible open-weight option for highly specialised solutions.

KiteFishAI positioned NanoI1 as a viable option for organisations whose most important requirements are customisation, security and specific operational considerations. The company stated that the model is intended to address specific operational needs rather than compete directly with large language models designed for a wide array of general tasks. TechGig reported that the announcement left out benchmark results, model parameters, pricing and hardware details, so those specifics remain undisclosed. The articles do not say what happens next beyond the launch itself.

stories.Headline: PwC and Harvey launch a Pillar Two tax assistant spanning 21 countries
stories.Summary:
PwC and Harvey built the Pillar Two Tax AI Assistant, a specialist research tool within Harvey, the companies announced on November 17, 2026. The Harvey Team published the announcement. The tool covers the OECD Pillar Two rules alongside country-specific material supplied by PwC network firms. It currently spans 21 countries. It is PwC's go-to tool for Pillar Two technical research.

More than 8,000 multinational groups are in scope of Pillar Two, the OECD framework that sets a 15% global minimum effective tax rate for groups with consolidated revenue of €750 million or more. According to the OECD, 45 jurisdictions have already taken steps to introduce the Global Anti-Base Erosion (GloBE) rules. The assistant draws only on vetted public sources: enacted and draft local legislation, tax authority guidance, and other official publications such as government consultations. Online sources are refreshed weekly, new documents are added monthly, and the content is reviewed quarterly. Users select it as a source in Harvey, filter by the countries they need, and use it alongside Harvey's other platform features.

The assistant has been rolled out to more than 17,000 PwC users across 21 countries and has recorded more than 70,000 user activities across more than 24,000 conversation threads. Monthly use grew roughly 17x, from about 700 activities in October 2025 to more than 12,000 in September 2026. A PwC Senior Associate, International Tax, Japan, said the module significantly improves the efficiency of their day-to-day Pillar Two work by helping them quickly navigate filing obligations, deadlines, and jurisdiction-specific requirements. A PwC Manager, International Tax, Germany, noted the module provides quick, well-structured overviews and access to relevant guidance and legislation, making country-specific research more efficient and effective. A Head of Tax of a multi-national group said they had a very positive experience with the module and would certainly recommend it to other clients looking for additional support and guidance on Pillar 2.

GloBE calculations generally start from each entity's financial accounts, as prepared for the parent's consolidated statements, and then require jurisdiction-specific adjustments. Some domestic regimes may substitute consolidated statements with local accounts. The OECD rules don't settle every local nuance, so teams must read the global rulebook alongside each country's legislation. The framework is global, but implementation is local, and those local differences decide what a group files, when it files, and how much top-up tax it owes. Working out exactly what data each country's rules require, and whether a group's data supports it, is often the hardest part.

Harvey will demonstrate the Pillar Two Tax AI Assistant and the Pillar Two Agent live at the PwC Tax Evolution Summit on November 18 in Madrid, Spain. The custom Harvey Agent tests each jurisdiction in a group against the FY2025 transitional CbCR safe harbours: the de minimis test, the simplified ETR test, and the routine profits test. Where a jurisdiction fails all three tests, the agent calculates an indicative top-up tax and shows where it would be collected, either locally or at the parent. The output is an Excel workbook showing the ETR working with live formulas, along with a self-contained interactive HTML view of the results. PwC has also rolled it out to clients, with positive feedback.

stories.Headline: Jastech wins South Korea world-class product status for its JFS humidity control solution
stories.Summary:
South Korean semiconductor humidity-control specialist Jastech said its second-generation humidity control solution, JFS, also called a Jet Flow Straightener, has been selected as a 2026 World-Class Product by South Korea's Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy and the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency, known as KOTRA. The selection marks the second consecutive year the company has earned the certification, following its first-generation N2 LPM product last year. The World-Class Product designation is a certification program under which the ministry and KOTRA award domestic products after comprehensively evaluating their global market competitiveness, technological prowess and growth potential. With the latest selection, Jastech has received official recognition of its technological competitiveness in the semiconductor humidity-control field.

JFS manages humidity by precisely controlling airflow inside semiconductor manufacturing processes, and applying it alongside N2 LPM can reduce cleanroom humidity, typically around 45% in ambient air, to as little as 1%. The first-generation N2 LPM laid the groundwork for yield improvement with nitrogen purge technology and can lower humidity to below 5%, while JFS adds precision airflow control for a higher level of humidity control. Jastech developed JFS for the first time in the world after about three years of research and development, and is currently supplying it to major global integrated device manufacturers. According to industry sources, Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix and U.S.-based Micron are known to have adopted Jastech's humidity-control solutions.

Cumulative sales of N2 LPM have now surpassed 300 billion won, approximately $225.4 million, and the company has set a goal of achieving 300 billion won in total company revenue by 2030 through expanded JFS supply. Ha Jung-min, director of Jastech's research institute and a vice president, said JFS is an optimal solution for improving yields in the increasingly ultra-fine and advanced HBM process environment. He said that as cumulative sales of the first-generation N2 LPM have comfortably exceeded 300 billion won, the company will make JFS a solid foundation for achieving 300 billion won in revenue by 2030. The certification is significant in that it comes as miniaturization of advanced memory processes such as HBM accelerates, and humidity management had been a relatively underappreciated process variable.

As circuit linewidths shrink and stacking becomes more advanced, yield sensitivity is rising, raising the possibility that equipment demand will grow as well. For Jastech, the certification amounts to securing a bridgehead to expand the global customer base built with its first-generation product to its second-generation product. However, the pace of capital investment by global semiconductor companies and the flow of equipment orders tied to HBM expansion plans are expected to act as variables before JFS translates into actual revenue contributions. As the company's 2030 revenue target of 300 billion won also exceeds the cumulative performance of its first-generation product, the speed at which the second-generation product penetrates the market is likely to be the key factor.

stories.Headline: Samsung develops custom high-bandwidth memory for Meta using a 2nm process
stories.Summary:
Samsung Electronics is reportedly developing custom high-bandwidth memory for the self-designed artificial intelligence chips of Meta. This technical collaboration was reported by Lillian Chen in Taipei on November 17, 2026. The project involves creating specialized memory components that can meet the specific needs of Meta's hardware. These custom memory solutions are intended to support the growing demands of advanced AI processing. The production of these custom components will require the use of Samsung Foundry's 2nm process for the base die.

This advanced manufacturing node allows for greater efficiency and performance in the memory architecture. By adopting the 2nm process, Samsung aims to provide the high speed and low power consumption required for AI. The integration of this specific process is a key requirement for the success of the custom HBM. The responsibility for the development of this hardware lies with the engineering teams at Samsung Electronics.

While the provided text does not include direct quotes, it indicates that Samsung is the primary developer for the memory. The company is working to align its foundry capabilities with the design specifications provided by Meta. This partnership highlights the shift toward customized hardware for large-scale artificial intelligence infrastructure. More to follow.

stories.Headline: Penguin Solutions unveils photonics-based HBM-class memory appliance for agentic AI workloads
stories.Summary:
Penguin Solutions unveiled the MemoryAI Photonic Appliance on November 16, 2026, to help agentic AI workloads. This new system is the first photonics-based HBM-class memory appliance designed to overcome GPU memory capacity constraints. The company showcased the appliance and its MemoryAI Photonic Memory Module at SC26 in Chicago. This hardware uses silicon photonics to let CPUs and GPUs share memory at high bandwidth memory data rates. The underlying module is built on the Marvell Photonic Fabric technology platform to deliver HBM-class performance.

The appliance targets terabytes-per-second data rates across multi-rack AI infrastructure using CXL 3.0 and Marvell photonic network interface cards. It supports up to 16 TB of DDR5 RDIMM memory and 576 GB of HBM3E memory per appliance. Total appliance bandwidth targets 57.6 Tbps and offers HBM Direct, HBM-DDR5 Cached, and DDR5 Direct access modes. The system allows memory to be located meters from GPUs rather than millimeters to expand available capacity. It integrates with the MemoryAI KV Cache Server and SMART CXL add-in cards for scalable, tiered memory.

Andy Mills, VP of Advanced Product Development at Penguin Solutions, said photonics provides a step-function change for AI. He stated that GPUs will have a direct way to access scale memory without hopping to a CPU. Preet Virk from Marvell said integrating their Photonic Fabric technology creates a path to high-capacity memory sharing. Virk noted that this approach is designed to improve accelerator utilization and increase the quality of tokens. Both executives believe these advancements will relieve stress on HBM memory and improve economic efficiency for inference.

The technology affects customers running agentic AI workloads that require high-speed data access for essential token generation. These users often face data bottlenecks that leave GPUs underutilized and contribute to the growing AI memory wall. One commenter questioned if the system is just memory with fast fiber NICs that might hide memory locations. This person compared the transparent access to a previous GPU model where local and attached memory were blurred. The appliance aims to help these users scale inference workloads without needing a proportional increase in GPU resources.

Localized ultra-fast HBM technology must sit within millimeters of the GPU, which limits capacity by package size and silicon I/O. Silicon photonics consumes less power than traditional copper interconnects and extends memory access across a photonic memory fabric. The MemoryAI Platform Architecture allows applications to access appliance memory as if it were directly attached without specialized routines. Memory can be statically or dynamically allocated through Penguin management software to handle specific workload requirements. This system complements existing GPU-attached HBM rather than replacing it to reduce pressure on high-speed memory.

Penguin Solutions plans to start sampling the MemoryAI Photonic Appliance to select customers in the second half of 2027. The articles do not state the specific pricing for the appliance or the MemoryAI Photonic Memory Module. There is no information regarding which specific customers have been selected for the initial sampling phase in 2027. The text does not mention the exact power consumption figures compared to the traditional copper interconnects mentioned. It remains open whether the transparent memory access will face the driver issues suggested by the online commenter.

stories.Headline: Mercor raises $750m Series D at $20bn valuation as annualised revenue passes $2bn
stories.Summary:
Mercor, a San Francisco company that pays doctors, lawyers, bankers and engineers to teach AI models how real work is done, announced in November 2026 a US$750m Series D at a US$20bn valuation, after its annualised revenue passed US$2bn in June 2026, up from US$1m two years earlier. The company was founded in 2023 by Brendan Foody, who is CEO, Adarsh Hiremath, who is Co-CEO, and Surya Midha, as an AI recruiting marketplace, and it found its market when AI labs needed experts rather than crowdworkers to write tasks, grade model responses and build verifiers for post-training. Its network counts more than five million domain experts, and it was paying out more than US$2m a day by March 2026, with contractors typically keeping 60% to 70% of gross billings. The Information reported US$614m in gross revenue for the first half of 2026, up 70% from the year before, and the company has more than 700 full-time employees as of November 2026. Felicis led a US$350m Series C at a US$10bn valuation in October 2025, and investors in the Series D include Benchmark, Felicis, Fundomo, funds managed by affiliates of Apollo, G Squared, General Catalyst, Glade Brook Capital, NVIDIA, Salesforce, Sapphire Ventures, StepStone Group, XTX Ventures and Zoom.

Mercor says it works with all of the top five AI labs and six of the Magnificent Seven tech companies, with OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Meta named in reports, and it is pushing into enterprises. In July 2026 it agreed to acquire Deeptune, an a16z-backed start-up backed by a US$43m Series A that has recreated hundreds of enterprise apps, including Salesforce, as environments, and whose team is joining Mercor's New York office. Its APEX benchmarks measure AI on economically valuable work, and in October 2026 AI outperformed 12 licensed CPAs on APEX-Accounting; Mercor also post-trained a 397bn-parameter open model with SkyRL, built at UC Berkeley with Anyscale, lifting its APEX-Agents score by 70% in relative terms, and released datasets and traces on Hugging Face. Foody said every job in the economy will need its own AI agents and every company will need a way to train and evaluate them on its own work, adding that Mercor spent the last two years building that infrastructure with the frontier labs and is now bringing it to enterprises. Hiremath said every company deploying AI needs to know whether it works and the answer is different for each one, because a model can score well on a public benchmark and still fail on the systems, policies and edge cases that define how a specific business runs, so Mercor builds custom benchmarks with each enterprise and uses them as the starting point for post-training.

The company's setbacks have been real: a late March 2026 supply-chain breach led Meta to pause all its work with Mercor while it investigated the security breach, according to WIRED. The next product is the training environment, a simulated workplace where an agent can practise a task and be scored, and Mercor said in a post on X that training AI to do real professional work requires covering the full distribution of apps, worlds and tasks across the economy, noting that Deeptune built the apps for the leading AI labs. Mercor's technology partners include Cognition, which co-launched the APEX-SWE software engineering benchmark with Mercor, Anyscale, Hugging Face, which hosts the datasets, model weights and evaluation traces released in September 2026, Modal, whose cloud infrastructure runs sandboxed agent trials, and Daytona, which provides sandboxed environments for agent training runs. The firm appears to have recovered from the breach and is pushing from frontier labs to enterprises.

stories.Headline: US blocks Chinese companies from accessing AI chips through overseas data centers
stories.Summary:
The United States government blocked Chinese companies from indirectly accessing advanced artificial intelligence chips. The Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security released these export control rules on the 18th. This move extends controls beyond direct exports to cover indirect routes through overseas data centers. The decision has put Samsung Electronics and SK hynix on alert. These Korean chipmakers are watching the situation closely.

Rules apply to data centers providing AI services exceeding 12 million total processing performance to China and other controlled countries. Supplying chips to these centers requires U.S. government approval, and existing services must obtain licenses within 90 days. Licensing requirements tightened for exports to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, and Brazil. The U.S. found Chinese companies avoided restrictions by placing data centers in Southeast Asia and elsewhere. New rules require contract manufacturers and packaging firms to verify design companies and parent companies.

The Bureau of Industry and Security is responsible for these new export control rules. The U.S. government stated that Chinese companies were avoiding restrictions by using overseas data centers. The Federal Reserve released a financial stability report on the 13th regarding AI data center investment. The Fed warned that risk exposure at large U.S. banks is estimated at about 1 trillion dollars. This exposure includes loans and credit extended to technology companies and data center developers.

Samsung could see shrinking orders in its foundry business which manufactures chips for Chinese-affiliated companies. SK hynix faces weaker demand for high-bandwidth memory it supplies to Nvidia. Both companies could be affected if Chinese companies find it harder to use Nvidia graphics processing units. Industry estimates suggest GPUs accessed by China through indirect routes account for 20 percent of global usage. Some observers say the near-term hit to earnings will be limited.

New debt for advanced computing infrastructure exceeded 680 billion dollars from January through October this year. This amount is more than five times the 130 billion dollars raised during all of 2023. Seven large technology companies, including Nvidia, Microsoft, and Oracle, owe over 3 trillion dollars in obligations. Samsung said last month that its entire 2027 high-bandwidth memory supply was already sold. SK hynix has secured substantial volumes through long-term supply contracts with major customers.

Future business environments for Samsung and SK hynix may be affected over the medium to long term. Slower demand growth could weigh on pricing power and profitability as companies expand production capacity. Some buyers might forfeit advance payments if market conditions experience a rapid downturn. The articles leave open whether data center operators will scale back or delay their investments. It remains unclear if the near-term earnings hit will truly be limited.

stories.Headline: Revolut deploys ChatGPT and Codex to cut coding time and automate financial crime screening
stories.Summary:
Revolut has adopted OpenAI's ChatGPT, API and Codex across its global operations, OpenAI reported on November 16, 2026, in a customer story titled "How Revolut raises ambition without lowering the bar." Revolut was built to challenge the way people interact with money, and that ambition now stretches across more than 40 markets and 800,000 businesses. Its consumer base has grown by 23% in the last 12 months, according to the article. One of Revolut's largest AI applications is a FinCrime agent powered by OpenAI models, which examines information, applies Revolut's rules and completes the defined process automatically. The release of GPT-5.5 was a turning point, when the models became capable and cost-effective enough for Revolut to delegate screening and investigation workflows entirely to the agent.

Codex has delivered a 30-60% reduction in coding time, from task start to feature merge, according to AI Lead David Abitbol. One engineer built an internal code-review service by delegating implementation tasks to multiple Codex agents. Revolut used one day to transform existing design-system documentation developed over roughly seven years into AI-readable context. More transactions are screened through the FinCrime agent without scaling investigators one for one. Revolut also developed a tool to build web UIs for internal apps and external-facing products.

Abitbol said Revolut has a systematic framework so anyone building with AI follows the same standards across development, A/B testing and business metric prediction, holding every engineer to the same quality standard. He said the biggest problem AI can tackle today is the scaling of humans versus the demand Revolut gets. Information Security Engineer Mo Amiri said the result translates directly into stronger protection and a more resilient system customers can trust. Senior Platform Engineer Dmitry Pitik said he realised he did not need a whole team of developers and could launch different agents and assign each a particular task. Pitik also said every developer is responsible for the code they produce and that they do not blindly trust AI.

Amiri said the most critical decision is always about accountability, and that if an AI tool suggests a code change, a human engineer needs to understand it well enough to stand by it. He said you earn real confidence in AI by making thoughtful decisions upfront and testing as you go. Global Head of Business Marketing Kim Maniovich said partnering with OpenAI enables Revolut to build solutions in a way that is lean, cost-efficient and tailored to how the company works. Maniovich said the average Revolut employee has three different jobs, and that month on month the targets get more aggressive but also more attainable. Senior Designer Dmytro Pavlov said Revolut can shift focus from things that are important but hard to do without AI to things that matter for customers.

According to one report cited in the article, over half of adults worldwide reported a scam encounter in 2025. For Revolut, every transaction creates another opportunity to identify suspicious activity, investigate potential risks and implement protections for customers. The volume of those transactions far outstrips the human resources available to any bank. In a phishing investigation, an analyst once had to gather an email, inspect its links and attachments, trace the sender and assemble the evidence manually. Amiri said that with stronger AI tools, those connections can be uncovered instantly and investigators can dig deeper into the questions that really matter.

Abitbol imagines a more conversational interface in which customers can ask Revolut to help with everyday financial tasks such as blocking a card, managing a subscription or finding ways to save for a trip. Pavlov sees the design challenge underneath that experience, turning complexity into something consistent, familiar and easy to use. Maniovich said she hopes Revolut can take the values it operates by every day, its unapologetic ambition and desire to never settle, and enable people to apply them to their own lives through the products it builds. The article says Revolut's next opportunity is to carry that combination of capability, judgment and design into the way customers interact with their money. The article does not say when any of these future products will launch.

stories.Headline: UNIST and Korea University researchers develop Q-Edge-popup to find smaller, noise-resistant quantum AI circuits
stories.Summary:
Researchers developed a technique to identify essential regions of complex quantum artificial intelligence circuits on November 18, 2026. This method cuts computational load and noise induced errors at the same time. A team led by Professor Yoon Sung-hwan of UNIST developed the process. They worked with a team led by Professor Kim Joong-heon of Korea University. The researchers mathematically proved that high performing small circuits exist inside large quantum neural networks.

The team created an algorithm called Q-Edge-popup to find these circuits in practice. They established a quantum strong lottery ticket hypothesis to account for the characteristics of quantum computation. The findings were presented at the CIKM 2026 conference in Rome from November 7 to 11. The research used a quantum neural network made of 3,840 rotation gates for simulation. This process requires sufficient quantum gates and specific initial settings to produce results close to target outputs.

First author Kwon Hong-gyun said high performing small circuits are likely to exist when specific conditions are met. He noted that these circuits do not exist in every single quantum circuit. Professor Yoon stated the key is searching for circuits that cut gate numbers while maintaining performance. He added that this work helps develop quantum AI models combining efficiency with stability. The research received support from the National Research Foundation of Korea and the Institute of Information & Communications Technology Planning & Evaluation.

The study affected the way researchers approach the slimming of quantum neural network models. In conventional AI, the strong lottery ticket hypothesis allows for slimming without changing weights. This theory could not be applied directly to quantum networks because gate order and measurement affect outcomes. The new algorithm scores each gate based on task performance to build a small circuit. Performance is then pushed higher by fine tuning only the parameters of the remaining gates.

The researchers confirmed the slimming effect through a computer simulation involving handwritten digit image classification. Keeping half of the gates produced a classification accuracy of 75.2 percent without changing any parameters. Training the selected gates raised accuracy to 79.4 percent, which approached the 81.3 percent of the full circuit. In mixed noise environments, the full circuit accuracy plunged 71.3 percentage points from 81.3 percent down to 10.0 percent. A circuit with 25 percent of gates held accuracy at 74.7 percent, down only 1.5 points from 76.2 percent.

The next step involves using these findings to create more stable and efficient quantum AI models. The Q-Edge-popup algorithm allows for the practical location of these high performing small circuits. The researchers proved that keeping a subset of gates with fixed parameters can maintain high accuracy. The articles do not state when these circuits will be used in real hardware. They also leave open how this technique will scale to even larger quantum neural networks.

stories.Headline: OpenAI launches ChatGPT for Sales with over 30 partner plugins
stories.Summary:
OpenAI introduced ChatGPT for Sales on November 17, 2026, according to a post on openai.com dated that day. The product is a new Sales experience built around a Sales plugin from OpenAI with dedicated skills for sellers. It also includes more than 30 new and enhanced partner plugins inside ChatGPT. OpenAI said the aim is to help every sales team understand customers better, spend less time on busywork and close more deals. The post said the tools let teams use information from the tools they already rely on to prepare for calls, tailor proposals and follow up faster.

The Sales plugin gives ready-to-use workflows for everyday sales work, from deciding which accounts to pursue to preparing for a call and drafting the follow-up. Partner plugins named in the post include Confluence, Guru and Seismic for learning sales processes and product updates, and ChatGPT Voice for rehearsing pitches and handling objections. Content tools named include ChatGPT Slides, Gamma, Figma and Canva, plus ChatGPT Sites for interactive demos or ROI calculators. Account tools named include Salesforce, HubSpot, Close CRM and monday CRM, and buyer-finding tools named include Apollo, Clay and Common Room, with Outreach and Salesloft for planning outreach. Call-note tools named include the Meetings plugin in ChatGPT, Gong, Otter.ai and Granola, Backstory is named for spotting deal risk, the Data plugin and Hex for analyzing sales data, and Docusign, Ironclad, PandaDoc and ServiceNow CPQ for quotes and agreements.

OpenAI said sellers can delegate work to their dot, an always-on agent in ChatGPT that can use the same plugins and customer context to prepare meeting briefs, track deal updates and bring relevant changes and proposed next steps for review. Sandeep Chellani, SVP and Head of Technology at The Michael J. Fox Foundation for Parkinson's Research, said the Salesforce Plugin for ChatGPT lets relationship builders uncover deeper insights about donor prospects and research partners and reduces the time and effort to gather and synthesize that information. Prof. Dr. Gunnar Gombert, Co-Founder and Managing Director of NeoBid, said the company uses HubSpot with ChatGPT for Sales to research real estate prospects, enrich CRM data, prioritize opportunities and prepare personalized outreach. Gombert estimated this reduces manual effort for these activities by around 65%, giving more time to help clients optimize energy procurement across their property portfolios. Sushanth Raman, CEO of Pallet, said ChatGPT for Sales and Rox are central to how the company operates and scales, and that Rox gives a clear view of the pipeline and surfaces deal risks early.

JR Harrell, EVP, Business Execution at Datasite, said Atlassian provides the connective tissue that allows OpenAI's frontier models to reason across the entire enterprise, and that grounding ChatGPT for Sales in the Teamwork Graph has democratized data. Jacob Tuwiner, Founder at Sculpted, said that in GTM the winners ship their best ideas before their competition, and that building in Clay for years meant clicking through menu after menu. Tuwiner said anyone can now use ChatGPT for Sales and Clay to ship a play in minutes that used to take an expert hours, days or weeks, and that Workflows shows every step instead of a giant table while Audiences takes the same play to a whole enterprise market. The post said availability of partner plugins and features varies by plan, region and workspace settings. It said ChatGPT Business and Enterprise admins can enable ChatGPT for Sales by opening the Admin Console, selecting their workspace and selecting Plugins, then making the Sales plugin and relevant partner plugins available for members to install or installing them by default.

The post said admins should review access to the required apps and the actions they can use, and that workspace members can complete any required account connections when prompted. It said OpenAI is continuing to build ChatGPT for Sales and the partner plugin ecosystem around the work sales teams do every day. OpenAI said its goal is to bring more of that work into ChatGPT, with connected tools and customer context that carries from finding an opportunity to preparing for a conversation and following through. The post listed related OpenAI announcements, including dots on September 29, 2026, the Admin plugin for ChatGPT Work and Codex on August 25, 2026, and an expanded Oracle partnership on October 27, 2026. The post said people can install the Sales plugin to get started and learn more about ChatGPT for Sales and the partner plugins.

The post did not give prices for ChatGPT for Sales or say which plans, regions or workspace settings include which partner plugins. It did not say when the more than 30 partner plugins became available or list all of them by name. It did not give a date for the next update to ChatGPT for Sales or say what that update will add. It did not say how many teams or sellers use the product. It did not give figures for time saved beyond NeoBid's estimate of around 65% less manual effort.

stories.Headline: Moritz assigns 90 percent of its workload to AI to handle complex cases within 24 hours
stories.Summary:
AI-native law firms are spreading across the United States to provide faster and cheaper legal services. These firms build their practices around artificial intelligence to improve overall efficiency. Nikkei reported on November 17 that these firms are growing rapidly. AI handles the legal work from the first draft through to the substance. Lawyers then verify and review the work produced by AI agents.

Moritz assigns 90 percent of its workload to AI to handle complex cases within 24 hours. Athena reduced a 20 hour complex case to two hours and 40 hour reviews to 40 minutes. Inside Practice notes pricing models include per-document rates, subscriptions, performance-based pricing, and flat fees. Norm AI raised 120 million dollars in a Series C round at a 1.2 billion dollar valuation. Norm Law is the firm associated with the parent company Norm AI.

Pamir Esas, chief executive of Moritz, said corporate fees are 80 to 90 percent lower than established firms. Richard Ferris, co-founder of Covenant, stated that every law firm will be AI-native in five years. Mike Schmidtberger joined Norm Law this year as chairman and partner. He was previously a chairman of the executive committee at Sidley Austin. These leaders emphasize that AI allows for much faster turnaround times.

Citigroup and Morgan Stanley are pressing large law firms to reduce fees due to AI efficiency. Junior associates are affected as their work is displaced and hiring for these roles is shrinking. A Citibank survey found 47 percent of firms saw summer internship hiring fall from a year earlier. Another 49 percent of firms expect next summer's internship hiring to fall further. Established law firms face pressure to cut rates to compete with AI-native firms.

The AI Firm Index showed 60 such firms worldwide as of September, doubling the number from six months prior. More than half of these firms are in the United States, Britain, Australia, and Germany. Crunchbase reported that legal-tech investment reached a record 4.586 billion dollars last year. GCVC is a venture fund for legal AI startups launched by current and former in-house counsel. Traditional firms previously relied on junior associates to prepare documents for senior lawyer sign-off.

Investment in legal-technology startups continues to increase as the use of AI widens in the legal field. The model of AI-native firms is currently spreading to Britain, Australia, and Germany. The articles do not state when the shift to AI-native firms will be complete. They do not specify which other countries might adopt this legal model. The reports leave open how traditional firms will adapt their hiring and billing.

stories.Headline: Jensen Huang resigns from Nvidia amid spying scandal as AI sentiment and markets slide
stories.Summary:
Jensen Huang quit Nvidia and admitted to an affair with a woman suspected of spying for China. These events, alongside high interest rates, rattled AI sentiment around November 18, 2026. Stocks, cryptocurrency, gold, and oil all declined together. Bitcoin fell 16 percent from the previous month to around 65,000 dollars. Gold plunged 6.36 percent in a single week.

The U.S. Commerce Department Bureau of Industry and Security implemented a 166-page rule on the 19th. It requires licenses for China to access U.S. AI semiconductor computing power through third-country data centers. Prior licenses are now required for advanced chip exports to Brazil, Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, and Thailand. The U.S. 10-year Treasury yield rose above 5 percent. The dollar index jumped to 103.695, its highest level since April last year.

Jensen Huang called himself a piece of shit before he resigned from his position. The U.S. government now requires approval for providing AI server performance to countries of security concern. China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs immediately signaled that it would retaliate against these new rules. The Federal Reserve may increase interest rates in December, which has frozen investor sentiment. The Remote Access Security Act in Congress is expected to move faster.

Retail investors bought 835.9 billion won of KODEX KOSDAQ150 Leverage ETFs while the KOSDAQ index fell 16.25 percent. These investors faced a 36.92 percent loss, while inverse ETFs returned between 19 and 21 percent. Bitcoin ETFs saw net outflows of 1.1 billion dollars over one week. Domestic semiconductor materials, parts, and equipment makers face increased short-term share price volatility. The KOSPI index fell below 5,000.

South Korean business groups invested 413.3 billion won in AI equity stakes during the first half of this year. The LG Group invested 265.6 billion won, and the Kakao Group invested 156.2 billion won. Kakao placed a 150 billion won bet on the large language model startup Upstage. Total AI investment over two and a half years reached 1.0972 trillion won. This follows a drop to 145.3 billion won last year from 538.5 billion won in 2024.

The market awaits the results of regular shareholder meetings next year regarding corporate governance change. Analysts are watching for improvements in board independence and capital allocation efficiency. South Korea must determine if it can maintain its technology gap against Chinese 8.6-generation facilities. The impact of the new U.S. licensing system on the AI supply chain remains uncertain. Short-term volatility for related stocks is considered unavoidable.
